items.stem: In a supernova nucleosynthesis positron-decay sequence, a parent titanium nucleus (A = 44, Z = 22) transforms via purely weak beta-plus transitions (u → d + e⁺ + νₑ) into a final nuclide with A = 44 and Z = 20, conserving baryon and lepton numbers at every vertex.
items.workedSolution: (a) ΔZ = 20 − 22 = −2. Final answer: −2. (b) N₀ = 44 − 22 = 22; N_f = 44 − 20 = 24. ΔN = N_f − N₀ = 2. Final answer: 2. (c) Accounting for ΔA = 0, charge conservation gives 2 weak beta transitions. Final answer: 2.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Z_final − Z_parent with sign to obtain −2.
Computes N = A − Z for parent and daughter and takes N_final − N_parent.
Evaluates correctly to 2.
Links single-quark flavour conversion to ΔZ = ±1 per weak beta step.
Evaluates correctly to 2.

items.stem: Inside a refractory-foil elastic alpha-scattering chamber, a 5.7 MeV alpha particle (charge +2e) comes momentarily to rest at minimum separation d before reversing direction in front of a tungsten nucleus (Z = 74, A = 184). Take k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
items.workedSolution: (a) Eₖ = 5.7 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹³ = 9.12 × 10⁻¹³ J. d = k(2e)(74e) / Eₖ = 3.73 × 10⁻¹⁴ m = 37.3 fm. Final answer: 37.3 fm. (b) R = 1.20 × (184)^(1/3) = 6.83 fm (< d, confirming pure electrostatic scattering). Final answer: 6.83 fm. (c) ρ = (184 × 1.661 × 10⁻²⁷) / ((4/3)π(6.83 × 10⁻¹⁵)³) = 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³. Final answer: 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Converts Eₖ to joules, equates Eₖ = k Q₁ Q₂ / d, and converts metres to femtometres.
Evaluates correctly to 37.3 fm.
Applies R = 1.20 × A^(1/3) fm.
Evaluates correctly to 6.83 fm.
Evaluates ρ = A u / ((4/3)πR³) in SI units.
Evaluates correctly to 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³.

items.stem: Nuclear geometry measurements in a refractory tantalum target scattering study direct 7.1 MeV alpha particles (Z₁ = 2) onto tantalum-181 (proton number Z = 73, mass number A = 181), using R = R₀ A^(1/3), R₀ = 1.20 fm = 1.20 × 10⁻¹⁵ m, and u = 1.661 × 10⁻²⁷ kg.

items.stem: During an optical spectroscopy run on a monochromatic sodium street-lighting discharge cell, sodium vapour atoms populate the first excited state at −3.07 eV, alongside a bound state at −5.23 eV below the zero-eV continuum limit. Constants: h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What minimum photon frequency is required to ionize the atom from the first excited state?
items.workedSolution: Energy needed to reach the continuum is ΔE = 3.07 eV = 4.91 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. Threshold frequency f = ΔE / h = 4.91 × 10⁻¹⁹ / (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴) = 7.41 × 10¹⁴ Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Uses f = |E| e / h to obtain 7.41 × 10¹⁴ Hz (B).

items.stem: A radiation detector in a positron-imaging elution calibrator operates in a steady background of 42 counts min⁻¹. A fresh gallium-68 specimen with half-life 68 min gives an initial uncorrected reading of 682 counts min⁻¹. Consider the detector response after 272 min. What total count rate (including background) does the detector record at t = 272 min?
items.workedSolution: Initial net count rate C₀ = 682 − 42 = 640 counts min⁻¹. Number of half-lives n = 272 / 68 = 4. Remaining net count rate C = 640 / 2^4 = 40 counts min⁻¹. Total recorded count rate = 40 + 42 = 82.0 counts min⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts background (640), divides by 2^4 (40), and adds 42 back to obtain 82.0 counts min⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides the initial total count rate directly by 2ⁿ without subtracting the background count rate first.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Correctly halves the background-subtracted net count rate but forgets to add the background count rate back to obtain the total detector reading.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides the net count rate by 2n instead of 2ⁿ.

items.stem: Quality-assurance logs in a neuroendocrine PET diagnostic unit record an initial population of 1.3 × 10¹⁴ gallium-68 nuclei with half-life 67.7 min. Consider the source after 50.1 min of continuous exponential decay. What is the activity of the sample, in becquerels (Bq), at t = 50.1 min?
items.workedSolution: T₁/₂ = 67.7 × 60 = 4.06 × 10³ s, so λ = ln 2 / T₁/₂ = 1.71 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹. Initial activity A₀ = λN₀ = 2.22 × 10¹⁰ Bq. At t = 50.1 min, A = A₀ e^(−λt) = 1.33 × 10¹⁰ Bq.

markScheme.criterion: Converts T₁/₂ to seconds, finds A₀ = λN₀, and evaluates A = A₀ e^(−λt) = 1.33 × 10¹⁰ Bq (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Fails to convert half-life from min to seconds (× 60) when computing A = λN in Bq (s⁻¹).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the initial activity A₀ = λN₀ at t = 0 without multiplying by the exponential decay factor e^(−λt).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses λ = 1 / T₁/₂ instead of λ = ln 2 / T₁/₂ when converting half-life to decay constant.

items.stem: A Minkowski worldline diagram for an intersecting proton-storage-ring hall shows primed axes (x′, ct′) of bunch A rest frame S′ moving at v = 0.8c relative to S, together with counter-circulating bunch B moving at u = −0.7c in S. What is the dimensionless velocity ratio u′ / c of counter-circulating bunch B measured in frame S′?

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes u and v with signs into u′/c = (u/c − v/c) / (1 − uv/c²) = −0.962 (C).

items.stem: Within a laser-produced ablation plasma plume, one-electron four-times ionized boron B⁴⁺ (Z = 5) ions populate principal shell n = 1 under the Bohr scaling law Eₙ = −13.6 Z² / n² eV relative to zero continuum energy (h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C).
items.workedSolution: (a) Eₙ = −13.6 × (5)² / (1)² = −340 eV. Ionization energy ΔE = 0 − Eₙ = 340 eV. Final answer: 340 eV. (b) ΔE = 340 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 5.44 × 10⁻¹⁷ J. f = ΔE / h = 5.44 × 10⁻¹⁷ / (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴) = 8.21 × 10¹⁶ Hz. Final answer: 8.21 × 10¹⁶ Hz. (c) λ = (3.00 × 10⁸) / (8.21 × 10¹⁶) = 3.66 nm. Final answer: 3.66 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Applies ΔE = 13.6 Z² / n² eV for the specified Z and n.
Evaluates correctly to 340 eV.
Converts ionization energy from eV to J and divides by Planck's constant h.
Evaluates correctly to 8.21 × 10¹⁶ Hz.
Uses λ = c / f and expresses the wavelength in nm to obtain 3.66 nm.

items.workedSolution: (a) Eₖ = qV = 2.00 × 10⁻¹⁶ J. v = √(2Eₖ / m) = 4.89 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹. Final answer: 4.89 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹. (b) λ = h / (mv) = 8.10 × 10⁻¹³ m = 8.10 × 10⁻⁴ nm. Final answer: 8.10 × 10⁻⁴ nm. (c) λ = 0.810 pm. Final answer: 0.810 pm.

items.stem: Energy-balance modelling of a pressurized-water thermal fission reactor fuel pin considers barium–krypton thermal fission of U-235: uranium nucleus (234.99345 u) + 1 thermal neutron (1.008665 u) → barium-141 nucleus (140.88354 u) + krypton-92 nucleus (91.90645 u) + 3 neutrons (each 1.008665 u). Use u = 931.5 MeV c⁻² and elementary charge e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the rest-mass decrease Δm, in atomic mass units (u), in a single fission reaction?
items.workedSolution: Summing reactant and product rest masses gives Δm = Σm_reactants − Σm_products = 0.186 u.

items.stem: Electrons are liberated from an alkali-metal sodium photocathode vacuum chamber (work function 2.36 eV) when monochromatic light of frequency 1.29 × 10¹⁵ Hz is incident in vacuum. Take h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.

items.stem: Coincidence spectroscopy in a Type Ia supernova light-curve nickel-cobalt-iron chain observes nickel (A = 56, Z = 28) decaying via purely weak beta-plus transitions (u → d + e⁺ + νₑ) into a product state at A = 56 and Z = 26. How many individual quark-level u → d weak beta transitions occur between the parent and final nucleus?
items.workedSolution: Each weak beta step flips exactly one quark inside a nucleon, changing Z by −1 while keeping A constant. Accounting for ΔA = 0 gives 2 weak quark transitions.

markScheme.criterion: Balances A and Z to identify 2 single-quark weak beta transitions (B).

items.stem: A collimated proton (charge +1e) carrying 5.7 MeV of kinetic energy undergoes direct head-on Coulomb backscattering from a stationary silver nucleus (Z = 47, A = 107) inside a silicon-diode nuclear recoil goniometer. Constants: k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻², e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the distance of closest approach d, in femtometres (fm)?
items.workedSolution: Initial kinetic energy Eₖ = 5.7 × 10⁶ × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 9.12 × 10⁻¹³ J. At the turning point, Eₖ = k(1e)(47e) / d, so d = (8.99 × 10⁹)(1)(47)(1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹)² / 9.12 × 10⁻¹³ = 11.9 fm.

markScheme.criterion: Equates Eₖ to k Q₁ Q₂ / d to obtain d = 11.9 fm (B).

items.stem: Radiochemical assay of a monazite mineral sand deposit tracks a thorium parent nuclide (A = 232, Z = 90) through sequential alpha and beta-minus decays into a daughter nuclide having A = 212 and Z = 82. How many beta-minus particles are emitted in this decay sequence?
items.workedSolution: Only alpha decay changes nucleon number A: Nα = (232 − 212) / 4 = 5. Proton balance gives 82 = 90 − 2(5) + Nβ⁻, so Nβ⁻ = 82 − 80 = 2.

markScheme.criterion: Finds Nα = 5 from ΔA / 4 and solves Z_f = Z_0 − 2Nα + Nβ⁻ to obtain Nβ⁻ = 2 (A).

items.stem: To verify wave-particle duality, a 390 V electron beam is directed perpendicularly onto polycrystalline graphite (110) planes (d = 1.23 × 10⁻¹⁰ m) at distance L = 0.13 m from a detector screen. Take first-order ring geometry sin θ = λ / d and r = L tan θ, with h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, mₑ = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg, and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the first-order diffraction angle θ, in degrees?
items.workedSolution: Electron wavelength λ = h / √(2mₑeV) = 6.22 × 10⁻¹¹ m. Using sin θ = λ / d = 0.506 yields θ = arcsin(0.506) = 30.4 °.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates λ = h / √(2mₑeV) and θ = arcsin(λ / d) = 30.4 ° (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Leaves arcsin(λ / d) in radians while labelling the answer in degrees.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inserts an extra factor of 2 in the denominator despite sin θ = λ / d being specified.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 in p = √(2mₑeV) when computing the electron de Broglie wavelength.

items.stem: A vapour cell in a cold-cathode neon spectroscopy tube contains neon gas whose the second excited state lies at −3.04 eV and whose adjacent bound level lies at −4.86 eV relative to the continuum threshold. Assume h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
items.workedSolution: (a) ΔE = 0 − (−3.04) = 3.04 eV. Final answer: 3.04 eV. (b) ΔE = 3.04 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 4.86 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. f = ΔE / h = 4.86 × 10⁻¹⁹ / (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴) = 7.34 × 10¹⁴ Hz. Final answer: 7.34 × 10¹⁴ Hz. (c) λ = c / f = (3.00 × 10⁸) / (7.34 × 10¹⁴) = 4.09 × 10⁻⁷ m. Converting to nanometres gives λ = 409 nm. Final answer: 409 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Finds ΔE = 0 − E_initial in eV to obtain 3.04 eV.
Converts ΔE to joules (× 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹) and applies f = ΔE / h.
Evaluates correctly to 7.34 × 10¹⁴ Hz.
Uses λ = c / f (or hc / ΔE) and converts metres to nanometres.
Evaluates correctly to 409 nm.

items.stem: Before testing an iodine-123 sample (half-life 13.2 h) in a gamma-camera collimator test rig, ambient background radiation registers 22 counts min⁻¹. Introducing the source raises the total detector reading to 1462 counts min⁻¹ initially, and monitoring continues for an elapsed interval of 66 h.
items.workedSolution: (a) C₀,net = 1462 − 22 = 1.44 × 10³ counts min⁻¹. Final answer: 1.44 × 10³ counts min⁻¹. (b) n = 66 / 13.2 = 5 half-lives. C_net = 1440 / 2^5 = 45.0 counts min⁻¹. Final answer: 45.0 counts min⁻¹. (c) C_total = 45 + 22 = 67.0 counts min⁻¹. Final answer: 67.0 counts min⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts background count rate from initial total count rate to obtain 1.44 × 10³ counts min⁻¹.
Identifies 5 elapsed half-lives and divides initial net count rate by 2^5.
Evaluates correctly to 45.0 counts min⁻¹.
Adds background count rate back to the remaining net count rate to obtain 67.0 counts min⁻¹.

Evaluates correctly to 8.79 × 10⁸ Bq.
Applies exponential decay law A = A₀ e^(−λt) with consistent time units.
Evaluates correctly to 1.94 × 10⁸ Bq.

items.stem: Observations of a solar prominence EUV grating spectrometer detect continuum photoionization edges from hydrogenic helium He⁺ (Z = 2) in excited shell n = 4, where discrete levels satisfy Eₙ = −13.6 Z² / n² eV. Constants: h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What minimum photon frequency is needed to remove the electron completely from excited shell n = 4?
items.workedSolution: Ionization energy from n = 4 is ΔE = 13.6 × 2² / 4² = 3.40 eV = 5.44 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. Threshold frequency f = ΔE / h = 8.21 × 10¹⁴ Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates f = (13.6 Z² / n²)(e / h) = 8.21 × 10¹⁴ Hz (C).

items.stem: Nuclear mass tables from an iron-peak maximum-stability mass trap list a stripped nickel-62 nucleus (A = 62, Z = 28) at rest mass 61.912927 u. Assume mₚ = 1.007276 u, mₙ = 1.008665 u, and u = 931.5 MeV c⁻². What is the binding energy per nucleon, in MeV, of this nickel-62 nucleus?
items.workedSolution: Neutron count N = 62 − 28 = 34. Mass defect Δm = 28(1.007276) + 34(1.008665) − 61.912927 = 0.585 u. Total binding energy B = Δm × 931.5 = 545 MeV. Binding energy per nucleon B / A = 545 / 62 = 8.80 MeV.

markScheme.criterion: Computes Δm = 0.585 u, B = 545 MeV, and B / A = 8.80 MeV (A).

items.stem: A collimated beam of thermal neutrons emerges from a heavy-water research-reactor velocity selector at speed 2200 m s⁻¹. Take h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s and mₙ = 1.675 × 10⁻²⁷ kg. What is the de Broglie wavelength, in nanometres (nm), of the thermal neutrons?
items.workedSolution: Momentum p = mv = (1.67 × 10⁻²⁷)(2200) = 3.69 × 10⁻²⁴ N s. De Broglie wavelength λ = h / p = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ / (3.69 × 10⁻²⁴) = 0.180 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates p and λ = h / p to obtain 0.180 nm (D).

items.stem: A nuclear data benchmark for a laser-driven proton–boron aneutronic fusion experiment specifies proton (1.007276 u) + boron-11 nucleus (11.006562 u) → 3 alpha particles (each of mass 4.001506 u) (with mass-energy equivalent u = 931.5 MeV c⁻² and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C).
items.workedSolution: (a) Δm = Σm_reactants − Σm_products = 9.32 × 10⁻³ u. Final answer: 9.32 × 10⁻³ u. (b) Q = 9.32 × 10⁻³ × 931.5 = 8.68 MeV. Final answer: 8.68 MeV. (c) Total nucleon number A = 12. Final answer: 12.

markScheme.criterion: Sums all reactant and product rest masses including particle multiplicities.
Evaluates correctly to 9.32 × 10⁻³ u.
Multiplies Δm in u by 931.5 MeV u⁻¹.
Evaluates correctly to 8.68 MeV.
Sums nucleon numbers across reactants (or products) to obtain 12.

items.workedSolution: Photon energy E = hf / e = (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ × 2.48 × 10¹⁵) / (1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹) = 10.3 eV. Maximum kinetic energy Eₖ,ₘₐₓ = E − Φ = 10.3 − 4.55 = 5.73 eV. Hence stopping potential Vₛ = 5.73 V.

markScheme.criterion: Computes eVₛ = hf − Φ to obtain Vₛ = 5.73 V (A).

items.stem: Along an evacuated drift-tube section of rest-frame length L₀ = 22.3 m in the laboratory hall, charged pions in a linear accelerator coast at uniform velocity v = 0.8c with pion rest-frame proper lifetime Δt₀ = 3.22 × 10⁻⁸ s. What contracted length L of the baseline L₀ is measured in the moving rest frame?
items.workedSolution: Lorentz factor γ = 1 / √(1 − 0.8²) = 1.67. Contracted length L = L₀ / γ = 22.3 / 1.67 = 13.4 m.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates γ = 1.67 and L = L₀ / γ = 13.4 m (D).

items.stem: In an ultra-high-vacuum time-of-flight spectrometer, monochromatic UV light of wavelength 142 nm strikes a clean tungsten sample of work function 4.55 eV. Use h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, and mₑ = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg. What is the threshold wavelength λ₀ above which no photoelectrons are emitted from this tungsten surface?
items.workedSolution: Threshold wavelength λ₀ = hc / Φ = (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ × 3.00 × 10⁸) / (4.55 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹) = 273 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates λ₀ = hc / Φ = 273 nm (A).

items.stem: During a lanthanide weak-decay spectrometer study, weak quark-flavour transitions (one alpha emission and weak beta-minus transitions (d → u + e⁻ + ν̄ₑ)) convert a parent cerium nucleus with A = 146, Z = 58 into a product nucleus with A = 142, Z = 59.
items.workedSolution: (a) ΔZ = 59 − 58 = 1. Final answer: 1. (b) N₀ = 146 − 58 = 88; N_f = 142 − 59 = 83. ΔN = N_f − N₀ = −5. Final answer: −5. (c) Accounting for ΔA = -4, charge conservation gives 3 weak beta transitions. Final answer: 3.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Z_final − Z_parent with sign to obtain 1.
Computes N = A − Z for parent and daughter and takes N_final − N_parent.
Evaluates correctly to −5.
Links single-quark flavour conversion to ΔZ = ±1 per weak beta step.
Evaluates correctly to 3.

items.stem: Elastic 180° backscattering in a Rutherford backscattering spectrometry (RBS) beamline sends a 4.5 MeV alpha particle (charge +2e) directly toward an immobile platinum target nucleus (Z = 78, A = 195), taking k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
items.workedSolution: (a) Eₖ = 4.5 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹³ = 7.20 × 10⁻¹³ J. d = k(2e)(78e) / Eₖ = 4.99 × 10⁻¹⁴ m = 49.9 fm. Final answer: 49.9 fm. (b) R = 1.20 × (195)^(1/3) = 6.96 fm (< d, confirming pure electrostatic scattering). Final answer: 6.96 fm. (c) ρ = (195 × 1.661 × 10⁻²⁷) / ((4/3)π(6.96 × 10⁻¹⁵)³) = 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³. Final answer: 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Converts Eₖ to joules, equates Eₖ = k Q₁ Q₂ / d, and converts metres to femtometres.
Evaluates correctly to 49.9 fm.
Applies R = 1.20 × A^(1/3) fm.
Evaluates correctly to 6.96 fm.
Evaluates ρ = A u / ((4/3)πR³) in SI units.
Evaluates correctly to 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³.

items.stem: Collimated electrons accelerated from rest across 480 V scatter coherently from thin polycrystalline aluminium foil (d = 2.04 × 10⁻¹⁰ m) onto an observation screen at L = 0.16 m. Use sin θ = λ / d and r = L tan θ with h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, mₑ = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg, and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
items.workedSolution: (a) p = √(2mₑeV) = 1.18 × 10⁻²³ N s. λ = h / p = 5.60 × 10⁻¹¹ m = 56.0 pm. Final answer: 56.0 pm. (b) sin θ = λ / d = 5.60 × 10⁻¹¹ / (2.04 × 10⁻¹⁰ m) = 0.275. θ = 15.9 °. Final answer: 15.9 °. (c) r = L tan θ = 0.16 × tan(15.9°) = 0.0457 m. Final answer: 0.0457 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses λ = h / √(2mₑeV) with SI values and converts to picometres.
Evaluates correctly to 56.0 pm.
Applies sin θ = λ / d and converts to degrees.
Evaluates correctly to 15.9 °.
Evaluates r = L tan θ using the screen distance L.
Evaluates correctly to 0.0457 m.

items.stem: During a lanthanide nuclear matter density check, a 6.8 MeV alpha beam (charge +2e) probes samarium-152 nuclei (Z = 62, A = 152). Assume a uniform spherical nucleus obeying R = R₀ A^(1/3), where R₀ = 1.20 fm = 1.20 × 10⁻¹⁵ m and u = 1.661 × 10⁻²⁷ kg.
items.workedSolution: (a) R = 1.20 × (152)^(1/3) = 6.40 fm. Final answer: 6.40 fm. (b) R = 6.40 × 10⁻¹⁵ m. Final answer: 6.40 × 10⁻¹⁵ m. (c) m = 152 × 1.661 × 10⁻²⁷ kg; V = (4/3)π(6.40 × 10⁻¹⁵)³. ρ = m / V = 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³. Final answer: 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes nucleon number A into R = R₀ A^(1/3).
Evaluates correctly to 6.40 fm.
Multiplies R in fm by 10⁻¹⁵ m fm⁻¹ to obtain 6.40 × 10⁻¹⁵ m.
Divides nuclear mass A u by spherical volume (4/3)πR³.
Evaluates correctly to 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³.

items.stem: During an optical spectroscopy run on a hollow-cathode lithium emission source, lithium vapour atoms populate the second excited state at −2.04 eV, alongside a bound state at −3.57 eV below the zero-eV continuum limit. Constants: h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. How much energy, in electron-volts (eV), is required to ionize a single atom from the second excited state?
items.workedSolution: Ionization energy from the second excited state to the continuum is ΔE = 0 − (−2.04) = 2.04 eV.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔE = 0 − (−2.04) = 2.04 eV (B).

items.stem: At a sealed ion-chamber radon monitor, a Geiger–Müller tube measures a mean background count rate of 34 counts min⁻¹ with no sample present. When a radon-220 (thoron) source of half-life 55.6 s is placed in front of the window at t = 0, the total recorded count rate is 434 counts min⁻¹. The detector is read again at t = 166.8 s. What total count rate (including background) does the detector record at t = 166.8 s?
items.workedSolution: Initial net count rate C₀ = 434 − 34 = 400 counts min⁻¹. Number of half-lives n = 166.8 / 55.6 = 3. Remaining net count rate C = 400 / 2^3 = 50.000000000000014 counts min⁻¹. Total recorded count rate = 50.000000000000014 + 34 = 84.0 counts min⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts background (400), divides by 2^3 (50.000000000000014), and adds 34 back to obtain 84.0 counts min⁻¹ (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides the initial total count rate directly by 2ⁿ without subtracting the background count rate first.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Correctly halves the background-subtracted net count rate but forgets to add the background count rate back to obtain the total detector reading.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides the net count rate by 2n instead of 2ⁿ.

items.stem: A freshly prepared vial in a cyclotron radiochemistry laboratory contains N₀ = 4.7 × 10¹⁴ undecayed nuclei of copper-64, whose half-life is 12.7 h. The vial is stored for t = 24 h before administration. What is the activity of the sample, in becquerels (Bq), at t = 24 h?
items.workedSolution: T₁/₂ = 12.7 × 3600 = 4.57 × 10⁴ s, so λ = ln 2 / T₁/₂ = 1.52 × 10⁻⁵ s⁻¹. Initial activity A₀ = λN₀ = 7.13 × 10⁹ Bq. At t = 24 h, A = A₀ e^(−λt) = 1.92 × 10⁹ Bq.

markScheme.criterion: Converts T₁/₂ to seconds, finds A₀ = λN₀, and evaluates A = A₀ e^(−λt) = 1.92 × 10⁹ Bq (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Fails to convert half-life from h to seconds (× 3600) when computing A = λN in Bq (s⁻¹).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the initial activity A₀ = λN₀ at t = 0 without multiplying by the exponential decay factor e^(−λt).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses λ = 1 / T₁/₂ instead of λ = ln 2 / T₁/₂ when converting half-life to decay constant.

items.stem: On the Minkowski spacetime diagram for a deep-space relativistic relay experiment, inertial frame S′ (patrol vessel S′) moves along the +x-axis of laboratory frame S at velocity v = 0.57c, while telemetry probe P moves along the x-axis with velocity u = 0.93c as measured in S. What is the dimensionless velocity ratio u′ / c of telemetry probe P measured in frame S′?

items.stem: Spectra recorded from a young supernova-remnant shock front show seven-times ionized oxygen O⁷⁺ (Z = 8) whose bound levels follow Eₙ = −13.6 Z² / n² eV relative to the ionization continuum. Consider ions prepared in excited shell n = 2 (with h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C).
items.workedSolution: (a) Eₙ = −13.6 × (8)² / (2)² = −218 eV. Ionization energy ΔE = 0 − Eₙ = 218 eV. Final answer: 218 eV. (b) ΔE = 218 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 3.48 × 10⁻¹⁷ J. f = ΔE / h = 3.48 × 10⁻¹⁷ / (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴) = 5.25 × 10¹⁶ Hz. Final answer: 5.25 × 10¹⁶ Hz. (c) λ = (3.00 × 10⁸) / (5.25 × 10¹⁶) = 5.71 nm. Final answer: 5.71 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Applies ΔE = 13.6 Z² / n² eV for the specified Z and n.
Evaluates correctly to 218 eV.
Converts ionization energy from eV to J and divides by Planck's constant h.
Evaluates correctly to 5.25 × 10¹⁶ Hz.
Uses λ = c / f and expresses the wavelength in nm to obtain 5.71 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Finds N = A − Z and evaluates Δm = Z mₚ + N mₙ − m_nuc.
Evaluates correctly to 0.0421 u.
Multiplies mass defect Δm in u by 931.5 MeV u⁻¹.
Evaluates correctly to 39.2 MeV.
Divides total binding energy B by nucleon number A to obtain 5.61 MeV.

items.stem: A beam of electrons starts from rest in a scanning electron microscope column and accelerates through a potential difference of 900 V in vacuum. Take h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, mₑ = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg, and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
items.workedSolution: (a) Eₖ = qV = 1.44 × 10⁻¹⁶ J. v = √(2Eₖ / m) = 1.78 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹. Final answer: 1.78 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹. (b) λ = h / (mv) = 4.09 × 10⁻¹¹ m = 0.0409 nm. Final answer: 0.0409 nm. (c) λ = 40.9 pm. Final answer: 40.9 pm.

markScheme.criterion: Equates ½mv² = qV and solves v = √(2qV / m).
Evaluates correctly to 1.78 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹.
Divides Planck's constant h by mv and converts metres to nanometres.
Evaluates correctly to 0.0409 nm.
Multiplies wavelength in nm by 1000 pm nm⁻¹ to obtain 40.9 pm.

items.stem: Within a red-giant helium-burning stellar core, nuclear power output originates from carbon-12 nucleus (11.996709 u) + helium-4 nucleus (4.001506 u) → oxygen-16 nucleus (15.990526 u). Constants: u = 931.5 MeV c⁻², e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. How much nuclear energy Q, in MeV, is released in one fusion event?
items.workedSolution: Mass decrease Δm = Σm_reactants − Σm_products = 7.69 × 10⁻³ u. Energy released Q = Δm × 931.5 = 7.16 MeV.

markScheme.criterion: Computes Δm = 7.69 × 10⁻³ u and Q = Δm × 931.5 = 7.16 MeV (A).

items.stem: In a photoelectric experiment using a freshly cleaved lithium vacuum target, a clean lithium surface of work function 2.93 eV is illuminated at frequency 9.26 × 10¹⁴ Hz. Use h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
items.workedSolution: (a) Φ = 2.93 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 4.69 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. f₀ = Φ / h = 4.69 × 10⁻¹⁹ / (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴) = 7.07 × 10¹⁴ Hz. Final answer: 7.07 × 10¹⁴ Hz. (b) Photon energy E = hf / e = 3.84 eV. Eₖ,ₘₐₓ = 3.84 − 2.93 = 0.907 eV. Final answer: 0.907 eV. (c) Vₛ = Eₖ,ₘₐₓ / e = 0.907 V. Final answer: 0.907 V.

markScheme.criterion: Converts Φ from eV to joules and applies f₀ = Φ / h.
Evaluates correctly to 7.07 × 10¹⁴ Hz.
Applies Einstein's photoelectric equation Eₖ,ₘₐₓ = hf/e − Φ.
Evaluates correctly to 0.907 eV.
Uses eVₛ = Eₖ,ₘₐₓ to obtain 0.907 V.

items.stem: Particle-nuclear tracking in an ophthalmic plaque ruthenium-rhodium beta source follows a ruthenium parent (nucleon number 106, proton number 44) undergoing purely weak beta-minus transitions (d → u + e⁻ + ν̄ₑ) to form a daughter nucleus (A = 106, Z = 46). What is the signed net change in neutron number ΔN = N_final − N_parent across the sequence?
items.workedSolution: Initial neutron number N₀ = 106 − 44 = 62; final neutron number N_f = 106 − 46 = 60. Thus ΔN = N_f − N₀ = −2.

markScheme.criterion: Uses N = A − Z to obtain ΔN = (106 − 46) − (106 − 44) = −2 (B).

items.stem: During an experiment in a heavy-element Coulomb-barrier scattering rig, an alpha particle (charge +2e) of kinetic energy 3.6 MeV is directed along a head-on trajectory toward a fixed lead nucleus (proton number Z = 82, nucleon number A = 208). Use k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the distance of closest approach d, in femtometres (fm)?
items.workedSolution: Initial kinetic energy Eₖ = 3.6 × 10⁶ × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 5.76 × 10⁻¹³ J. At the turning point, Eₖ = k(2e)(82e) / d, so d = (8.99 × 10⁹)(2)(82)(1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹)² / 5.76 × 10⁻¹³ = 65.5 fm.

markScheme.criterion: Equates Eₖ to k Q₁ Q₂ / d to obtain d = 65.5 fm (D).

items.stem: Mass-spectrometric analysis of a spent-fuel isotopic Safeguards assay identifies a decay chain starting from plutonium (A = 240, Z = 94) and ending at a daughter nucleus (A = 220, Z = 86) via alpha and beta-minus steps only. How many beta-minus particles are emitted in this decay sequence?
items.workedSolution: Only alpha decay changes nucleon number A: Nα = (240 − 220) / 4 = 5. Proton balance gives 86 = 94 − 2(5) + Nβ⁻, so Nβ⁻ = 86 − 84 = 2.

markScheme.criterion: Finds Nα = 5 from ΔA / 4 and solves Z_f = Z_0 − 2Nα + Nβ⁻ to obtain Nβ⁻ = 2 (B).

items.stem: In an evacuated electron-diffraction tube, electrons accelerated from rest through 260 V pass through polycrystalline graphite (100) planes of interplanar spacing d = 2.13 × 10⁻¹⁰ m and form concentric bright rings on a phosphor screen L = 0.14 m behind the foil. Use sin θ = λ / d and ring radius r = L tan θ, taking h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, mₑ = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg, and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the radius r of the first-order bright diffraction ring on the screen?
items.workedSolution: λ = h / √(2mₑeV) = 7.62 × 10⁻¹¹ m. Then sin θ = λ / d = 0.358, giving θ = 20.9 ° and ring radius r = L tan θ = 0.14 × tan(20.9°) = 0.0536 m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds λ = 7.62 × 10⁻¹¹ m, θ = 20.9°, and r = L tan θ = 0.0536 m (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the full diameter 2r of the diffraction ring instead of its radius r.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 inside p = √(2mₑeV), overestimating λ and ring radius by √2.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the diffraction ratio as d / λ instead of λ / d.

items.stem: Inside a hollow-cathode lithium emission source, discrete electronic levels of lithium vapour include the second excited state at −2.01 eV and an adjacent bound level at −3.52 eV relative to the zero-energy ionization continuum. Take h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
items.workedSolution: (a) ΔE = 0 − (−2.01) = 2.01 eV. Final answer: 2.01 eV. (b) ΔE = 2.01 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 3.22 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. f = ΔE / h = 3.22 × 10⁻¹⁹ / (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴) = 4.85 × 10¹⁴ Hz. Final answer: 4.85 × 10¹⁴ Hz. (c) λ = c / f = (3.00 × 10⁸) / (4.85 × 10¹⁴) = 6.18 × 10⁻⁷ m. Converting to nanometres gives λ = 618 nm. Final answer: 618 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Finds ΔE = 0 − E_initial in eV to obtain 2.01 eV.
Converts ΔE to joules (× 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹) and applies f = ΔE / h.
Evaluates correctly to 4.85 × 10¹⁴ Hz.
Uses λ = c / f (or hc / ΔE) and converts metres to nanometres.
Evaluates correctly to 618 nm.

items.stem: At a hospital nuclear-medicine dispenser, a Geiger–Müller tube measures a mean background count rate of 34 counts min⁻¹ with no sample present. When a technetium-99m source of half-life 6 h is placed in front of the window at t = 0, the total recorded count rate is 834 counts min⁻¹. The detector is read again at t = 24 h.
items.workedSolution: (a) C₀,net = 834 − 34 = 800 counts min⁻¹. Final answer: 800 counts min⁻¹. (b) n = 24 / 6 = 4 half-lives. C_net = 800 / 2^4 = 50.0 counts min⁻¹. Final answer: 50.0 counts min⁻¹. (c) C_total = 50 + 34 = 84.0 counts min⁻¹. Final answer: 84.0 counts min⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts background count rate from initial total count rate to obtain 800 counts min⁻¹.
Identifies 4 elapsed half-lives and divides initial net count rate by 2^4.
Evaluates correctly to 50.0 counts min⁻¹.
Adds background count rate back to the remaining net count rate to obtain 84.0 counts min⁻¹.

parts.prompt: Determine the initial corrected count rate due solely to the technetium-99m source at t = 0.
Calculate the corrected count rate from the source alone at t = 24 h.
State the total count rate displayed by the detector at t = 24 h.

items.stem: A freshly prepared vial in a neuroendocrine PET diagnostic unit contains N₀ = 1.4 × 10¹⁵ undecayed nuclei of gallium-68, whose half-life is 67.7 min. The vial is stored for t = 39.3 min before administration.

markScheme.criterion: Converts T₁/₂ from min to seconds and applies λ = ln 2 / T₁/₂.
Evaluates correctly to 1.71 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹.
Multiplies λ in s⁻¹ by N₀ using A₀ = λN₀.
Evaluates correctly to 2.39 × 10¹¹ Bq.
Applies exponential decay law A = A₀ e^(−λt) with consistent time units.
Evaluates correctly to 1.60 × 10¹¹ Bq.

parts.prompt: Show the conversion of the half-life to seconds and calculate the decay constant λ in s⁻¹.
Calculate the initial activity A₀ of the sample, in Bq, at t = 0.
Determine the activity A of the sample, in Bq, after t = 39.3 min.

Applies u′ = (u − v) / (1 − uv/c²) preserving algebraic signs.
Evaluates correctly to −0.921.

items.stem: Spectra recorded from a young supernova-remnant shock front show seven-times ionized oxygen O⁷⁺ (Z = 8) whose bound levels follow Eₙ = −13.6 Z² / n² eV relative to the ionization continuum. Consider ions prepared in excited shell n = 2 (with h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C). What is the series-limit (maximum) photon wavelength that can photoionize this species from excited shell n = 2?
items.workedSolution: Initial level energy Eₙ = −13.6 × 8² / 2² = −218 eV. Ionization requires ΔE = 218 eV = 3.48 × 10⁻¹⁷ J. Maximum ionizing wavelength λ = hc / ΔE = 5.71 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Computes ΔE = 13.6 Z² / n² eV and λ = hc / ΔE = 5.71 nm (A).

items.stem: Data from a heavy-hydrogen ion-trap mass measurement give the bare nuclear rest mass of deuterium (nucleon number A = 2, proton number Z = 1) as 2.013553 u. Take free proton mass mₚ = 1.007276 u, free neutron mass mₙ = 1.008665 u, and atomic mass energy equivalent u = 931.5 MeV c⁻². What is the binding energy per nucleon, in MeV, of this deuterium nucleus?
items.workedSolution: Neutron count N = 2 − 1 = 1. Mass defect Δm = 1(1.007276) + 1(1.008665) − 2.013553 = 2.39 × 10⁻³ u. Total binding energy B = Δm × 931.5 = 2.22 MeV. Binding energy per nucleon B / A = 2.22 / 2 = 1.11 MeV.

markScheme.criterion: Computes Δm = 2.39 × 10⁻³ u, B = 2.22 MeV, and B / A = 1.11 MeV (C).

items.stem: In crystallographic neutron scattering using a heavy-water research-reactor velocity selector, thermal neutrons travel at a steady speed of 3100 m s⁻¹. Use h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s and mₙ = 1.675 × 10⁻²⁷ kg. What is the de Broglie wavelength, in nanometres (nm), of the thermal neutrons?
items.workedSolution: Momentum p = mv = (1.67 × 10⁻²⁷)(3100) = 5.19 × 10⁻²⁴ N s. De Broglie wavelength λ = h / p = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ / (5.19 × 10⁻²⁴) = 0.128 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates p and λ = h / p to obtain 0.128 nm (C).

options.label: B

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Treats the massive particle as a massless photon using λ = hc / E instead of λ = h / p.

items.stem: Calorimetric analysis of a spherical-tokamak deuterium-burn diagnostic shot evaluates the single-event nuclear fusion step 2 deuterons (each of mass 2.013553 u) → triton (3.015501 u) + proton (1.007276 u) (take u = 931.5 MeV c⁻², e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C).
items.workedSolution: (a) Δm = Σm_reactants − Σm_products = 4.33 × 10⁻³ u. Final answer: 4.33 × 10⁻³ u. (b) Q = 4.33 × 10⁻³ × 931.5 = 4.03 MeV. Final answer: 4.03 MeV. (c) Total nucleon number A = 4. Final answer: 4.

markScheme.criterion: Sums all reactant and product rest masses including particle multiplicities.
Evaluates correctly to 4.33 × 10⁻³ u.
Multiplies Δm in u by 931.5 MeV u⁻¹.
Evaluates correctly to 4.03 MeV.
Sums nucleon numbers across reactants (or products) to obtain 4.

items.stem: To calibrate an electroscope-mounted clean zinc UV plate, ultraviolet photons at 2.06 × 10¹⁵ Hz irradiate a zinc electrode having Φ = 4.33 eV. Constants: h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the threshold frequency f₀ of the zinc surface?
items.workedSolution: Work function Φ = 4.33 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 6.93 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. Threshold frequency f₀ = Φ / h = 6.93 × 10⁻¹⁹ / (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴) = 1.04 × 10¹⁵ Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates f₀ = Φ / h = 1.04 × 10¹⁵ Hz (D).

items.stem: Relative to an Earth mountain observatory, atmospheric cosmic-ray muons travel at constant speed v = 0.96c across a vertical atmospheric column of stationary-frame proper length L₀ = 4800 m, while the muon rest-frame mean lifetime is Δt₀ = 2.2 × 10⁻⁶ s. What dilated time interval Δt corresponds to Δt₀ in the stationary observer frame?
items.workedSolution: Lorentz factor γ = 1 / √(1 − 0.96²) = 3.57. Dilated time interval Δt = γ Δt₀ = 3.57 × 2.2 × 10⁻⁶ = 7.86 × 10⁻⁶ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates γ = 3.57 and Δt = γ Δt₀ = 7.86 × 10⁻⁶ s (A).

items.stem: Photoemission from an electroscope-mounted clean zinc UV plate is driven by narrowband 112 nm UV light incident on zinc having work function Φ = 4.33 eV. Take h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, and mₑ = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg. What is the maximum speed of the emitted photoelectrons?
items.workedSolution: Incident photon energy E = hc / λ = 1.78 × 10⁻¹⁸ J; work function Φ = 4.33 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 6.93 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. Thus Eₖ,ₘₐₓ = 1.08 × 10⁻¹⁸ J, giving vₘₐₓ = √(2Eₖ,ₘₐₓ / mₑ) = 1.54 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes Eₖ,ₘₐₓ = hc/λ − Φ and vₘₐₓ = √(2Eₖ,ₘₐₓ / mₑ) = 1.54 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: The energy-level diagram illustrates radiative transitions in potassium vapour within a heated alkali-metal potassium absorption cell. An atom initially occupies the first excited state at energy −2.73 eV (with a nearby level at −4.34 eV and ionization at zero eV). Take h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What minimum photon frequency is required to ionize the atom from the first excited state?
items.workedSolution: Energy needed to reach the continuum is ΔE = 2.73 eV = 4.37 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. Threshold frequency f = ΔE / h = 4.37 × 10⁻¹⁹ / (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴) = 6.59 × 10¹⁴ Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Uses f = |E| e / h to obtain 6.59 × 10¹⁴ Hz (D).

items.stem: During an assay in a thyroid-therapy assay counter, background radiation alone accounts for 30 counts min⁻¹. With an iodine-131 source (half-life 8 d) fixed in position, the initial total count rate is 1054 counts min⁻¹; measurements are repeated 40 d later. What total count rate (including background) does the detector record at t = 40 d?
items.workedSolution: Initial net count rate C₀ = 1054 − 30 = 1024 counts min⁻¹. Number of half-lives n = 40 / 8 = 5. Remaining net count rate C = 1024 / 2^5 = 32 counts min⁻¹. Total recorded count rate = 32 + 30 = 62.0 counts min⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts background (1024), divides by 2^5 (32), and adds 30 back to obtain 62.0 counts min⁻¹ (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides the initial total count rate directly by 2ⁿ without subtracting the background count rate first.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Correctly halves the background-subtracted net count rate but forgets to add the background count rate back to obtain the total detector reading.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides the net count rate by 2n instead of 2ⁿ.

items.stem: A sealed capsule in an alpha-radiopharmaceutical dosimetry lab holds 7.4 × 10¹⁴ unstable nuclei of radium-223 (T₁/₂ = 11.4 d), decaying exponentially over a transport interval of 13.5 d. What is the initial activity A₀ of the sample, in Bq, at t = 0?
items.workedSolution: Converting half-life to SI seconds: T₁/₂ = 11.4 × 86400 = 9.85 × 10⁵ s. Decay constant λ = ln 2 / T₁/₂ = 7.04 × 10⁻⁷ s⁻¹. Initial activity A₀ = λN₀ = 5.21 × 10⁸ Bq.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates λ = ln 2 / (11.4 × 86400) and A₀ = λN₀ = 5.21 × 10⁸ Bq (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Leaves T₁/₂ in d instead of converting to seconds when evaluating A₀ = (ln 2 / T₁/₂) N₀ in Bq.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor ln 2 ≈ 0.693 in λ = ln 2 / T₁/₂.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes the decayed activity at elapsed time t instead of A₀ at t = 0.

items.stem: Observations of a solar-flare coronal magnetic loop detect continuum photoionization edges from six-times ionized nitrogen N⁶⁺ (Z = 7) in outer bound shell n = 5, where discrete levels satisfy Eₙ = −13.6 Z² / n² eV. Constants: h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
items.workedSolution: (a) Eₙ = −13.6 × (7)² / (5)² = −26.7 eV. Ionization energy ΔE = 0 − Eₙ = 26.7 eV. Final answer: 26.7 eV. (b) ΔE = 26.7 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 4.26 × 10⁻¹⁸ J. f = ΔE / h = 4.26 × 10⁻¹⁸ / (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴) = 6.43 × 10¹⁵ Hz. Final answer: 6.43 × 10¹⁵ Hz. (c) λ = (3.00 × 10⁸) / (6.43 × 10¹⁵) = 46.6 nm. Final answer: 46.6 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Applies ΔE = 13.6 Z² / n² eV for the specified Z and n.
Evaluates correctly to 26.7 eV.
Converts ionization energy from eV to J and divides by Planck's constant h.
Evaluates correctly to 6.43 × 10¹⁵ Hz.
Uses λ = c / f and expresses the wavelength in nm to obtain 46.6 nm.

items.stem: Vacuum-emitted electrons in a low-energy electron diffraction (LEED) gun gain kinetic energy across a 650 V accelerating anode from negligible initial speed. Assume h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, mₑ = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg, and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
items.workedSolution: (a) Eₖ = qV = 1.04 × 10⁻¹⁶ J. v = √(2Eₖ / m) = 1.51 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹. Final answer: 1.51 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹. (b) λ = h / (mv) = 4.82 × 10⁻¹¹ m = 0.0482 nm. Final answer: 0.0482 nm. (c) λ = 48.2 pm. Final answer: 48.2 pm.

markScheme.criterion: Equates ½mv² = qV and solves v = √(2qV / m).
Evaluates correctly to 1.51 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹.
Divides Planck's constant h by mv and converts metres to nanometres.
Evaluates correctly to 0.0482 nm.
Multiplies wavelength in nm by 1000 pm nm⁻¹ to obtain 48.2 pm.

items.stem: In a heavy-water CANDU fuel bundle, the exothermic nuclear fission reaction is: uranium nucleus (234.99345 u) + 1 thermal neutron (1.008665 u) → caesium-141 nucleus (140.8890 u) + rubidium-93 nucleus (92.9017 u) + 2 neutrons (each 1.008665 u). Take atomic mass energy conversion u = 931.5 MeV c⁻² and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. How much nuclear energy Q, in MeV, is released in one fission event?
items.workedSolution: Mass decrease Δm = Σm_reactants − Σm_products = 0.194 u. Energy released Q = Δm × 931.5 = 181 MeV.

markScheme.criterion: Computes Δm = 0.194 u and Q = Δm × 931.5 = 181 MeV (C).

items.stem: Monochromatic electromagnetic radiation of frequency 1.54 × 10¹⁵ Hz strikes a barium-coated electron-tube emitter whose work function is 2.52 eV. Take h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
items.workedSolution: (a) Φ = 2.52 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 4.03 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. f₀ = Φ / h = 4.03 × 10⁻¹⁹ / (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴) = 6.08 × 10¹⁴ Hz. Final answer: 6.08 × 10¹⁴ Hz. (b) Photon energy E = hf / e = 6.38 eV. Eₖ,ₘₐₓ = 6.38 − 2.52 = 3.86 eV. Final answer: 3.86 eV. (c) Vₛ = Eₖ,ₘₐₓ / e = 3.86 V. Final answer: 3.86 V.

markScheme.criterion: Converts Φ from eV to joules and applies f₀ = Φ / h.
Evaluates correctly to 6.08 × 10¹⁴ Hz.
Applies Einstein's photoelectric equation Eₖ,ₘₐₓ = hf/e − Φ.
Evaluates correctly to 3.86 eV.
Uses eVₛ = Eₖ,ₘₐₓ to obtain 3.86 V.

items.stem: Electrostatic repulsion inside a Rutherford backscattering spectrometry (RBS) beamline halts a head-on alpha particle (charge +2e) of initial energy 6.5 MeV at closest approach d from a stationary platinum nucleus (Z = 78, A = 195). Assume k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the distance of closest approach d, in femtometres (fm)?
items.workedSolution: Initial kinetic energy Eₖ = 6.5 × 10⁶ × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 1.04 × 10⁻¹² J. At the turning point, Eₖ = k(2e)(78e) / d, so d = (8.99 × 10⁹)(2)(78)(1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹)² / 1.04 × 10⁻¹² = 34.5 fm.

markScheme.criterion: Equates Eₖ to k Q₁ Q₂ / d to obtain d = 34.5 fm (B).

items.stem: In a neutron-moisture gauge isotopic capsule, a parent californium nucleus with nucleon number A = 252 and proton number Z = 98 decays solely by alpha and beta-minus emissions along the stability-chart path shown until reaching a daughter nuclide with A = 236 and Z = 92. What is the net change in neutron number ΔN = N_final − N_parent across the entire chain?
items.workedSolution: Parent neutron number N₀ = 252 − 98 = 154. Final neutron number N_f = 236 − 92 = 144. Therefore ΔN = N_f − N₀ = −10.

items.stem: In an evacuated electron-diffraction tube, electrons accelerated from rest through 320 V pass through sputtered polycrystalline silver film of interplanar spacing d = 2.36 × 10⁻¹⁰ m and form concentric bright rings on a phosphor screen L = 0.17 m behind the foil. Use sin θ = λ / d and ring radius r = L tan θ, taking h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, mₑ = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg, and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the first-order diffraction angle θ, in degrees?
items.workedSolution: Electron wavelength λ = h / √(2mₑeV) = 6.86 × 10⁻¹¹ m. Using sin θ = λ / d = 0.291 yields θ = arcsin(0.291) = 16.9 °.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates λ = h / √(2mₑeV) and θ = arcsin(λ / d) = 16.9 ° (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Leaves arcsin(λ / d) in radians while labelling the answer in degrees.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inserts an extra factor of 2 in the denominator despite sin θ = λ / d being specified.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 in p = √(2mₑeV) when computing the electron de Broglie wavelength.

items.stem: Empirical nuclear-size analysis in a magic-neutron zirconium radius determination examines zirconium-90 (Z = 40, A = 90) illuminated by 6.3 MeV alpha particles (Z₁ = 2), taking R = R₀ A^(1/3), R₀ = 1.20 fm = 1.20 × 10⁻¹⁵ m, and u = 1.661 × 10⁻²⁷ kg. Assuming nuclear mass m ≈ A u, what is the nuclear matter density ρ of this zirconium-90 nucleus?
items.workedSolution: Since R = R₀ A^(1/3), V = (4/3)πR³ = (4/3)π R₀³ A. Thus ρ = (A u) / ((4/3)π R₀³ A) = 3u / (4π R₀³) = 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Computes ρ = A u / ((4/3)πR³) = 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³ (A).

items.stem: A vapour cell in a heated alkali-metal potassium absorption cell contains potassium vapour whose the first excited state lies at −2.69 eV and whose adjacent bound level lies at −4.25 eV relative to the continuum threshold. Assume h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
items.workedSolution: (a) ΔE = 0 − (−2.69) = 2.69 eV. Final answer: 2.69 eV. (b) ΔE = 2.69 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 4.30 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. f = ΔE / h = 4.30 × 10⁻¹⁹ / (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴) = 6.49 × 10¹⁴ Hz. Final answer: 6.49 × 10¹⁴ Hz. (c) λ = c / f = (3.00 × 10⁸) / (6.49 × 10¹⁴) = 4.62 × 10⁻⁷ m. Converting to nanometres gives λ = 462 nm. Final answer: 462 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Finds ΔE = 0 − E_initial in eV to obtain 2.69 eV.
Converts ΔE to joules (× 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹) and applies f = ΔE / h.
Evaluates correctly to 6.49 × 10¹⁴ Hz.
Uses λ = c / f (or hc / ΔE) and converts metres to nanometres.
Evaluates correctly to 462 nm.

items.stem: During an assay in an alpha-scintillation foil monitor, background radiation alone accounts for 30 counts min⁻¹. With a polonium-210 source (half-life 138 d) fixed in position, the initial total count rate is 158 counts min⁻¹; measurements are repeated 276 d later.
items.workedSolution: (a) C₀,net = 158 − 30 = 128 counts min⁻¹. Final answer: 128 counts min⁻¹. (b) n = 276 / 138 = 2 half-lives. C_net = 128 / 2^2 = 32.0 counts min⁻¹. Final answer: 32.0 counts min⁻¹. (c) C_total = 32 + 30 = 62.0 counts min⁻¹. Final answer: 62.0 counts min⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts background count rate from initial total count rate to obtain 128 counts min⁻¹.
Identifies 2 elapsed half-lives and divides initial net count rate by 2^2.
Evaluates correctly to 32.0 counts min⁻¹.
Adds background count rate back to the remaining net count rate to obtain 62.0 counts min⁻¹.

parts.prompt: Determine the initial corrected count rate due solely to the polonium-210 source at t = 0.

State the total count rate displayed by the detector at t = 276 d.

Evaluates correctly to 3.72 × 10⁹ Bq.
Applies exponential decay law A = A₀ e^(−λt) with consistent time units.
Evaluates correctly to 5.22 × 10⁸ Bq.

items.stem: High-resolution UV/X-ray grating data from a helical stellarator edge-pedestal plasma probe hydrogen-like lithium Li²⁺ (Z = 3), modelled by Eₙ = −13.6 Z² / n² eV. For an ion initially in excited shell n = 3, use h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What minimum photon frequency is needed to remove the electron completely from excited shell n = 3?
items.workedSolution: Ionization energy from n = 3 is ΔE = 13.6 × 3² / 3² = 13.6 eV = 2.18 × 10⁻¹⁸ J. Threshold frequency f = ΔE / h = 3.28 × 10¹⁵ Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates f = (13.6 Z² / n²)(e / h) = 3.28 × 10¹⁵ Hz (D).

items.stem: In a thermal-fission daughter mass evaluation, a bare barium-141 nucleus with A = 141 and Z = 56 is measured to have rest mass 140.88354 u. Using mₚ = 1.007276 u, mₙ = 1.008665 u, and u = 931.5 MeV c⁻²: What is the binding energy per nucleon, in MeV, of this barium-141 nucleus?
items.workedSolution: Neutron count N = 141 − 56 = 85. Mass defect Δm = 56(1.007276) + 85(1.008665) − 140.88354 = 1.26 u. Total binding energy B = Δm × 931.5 = 1.17 × 10³ MeV. Binding energy per nucleon B / A = 1.17 × 10³ / 141 = 8.33 MeV.

markScheme.criterion: Computes Δm = 1.26 u, B = 1.17 × 10³ MeV, and B / A = 8.33 MeV (C).

items.stem: Vacuum-emitted alpha particles in an electrostatic helium-ion accelerator stage gain kinetic energy across a 480 V accelerating anode from negligible initial speed. Assume h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, mα = 6.644 × 10⁻²⁷ kg, and charge +2e with e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the de Broglie wavelength, in nanometres (nm), of the alpha particles?
items.workedSolution: Kinetic energy Eₖ = qV = 1.54 × 10⁻¹⁶ J. Momentum p = √(2mEₖ) = 1.43 × 10⁻²¹ N s. De Broglie wavelength λ = h / p = 4.64 × 10⁻⁴ nm.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates p and λ = h / p to obtain 4.64 × 10⁻⁴ nm (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 inside p = √(2mEₖ), computing λ = h / √(mEₖ).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats the massive particle as a massless photon using λ = hc / E instead of λ = h / p.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies wavelength by an erroneous factor of 2.

items.stem: In a dense plasma-focus D–D neutron generator, the exothermic nuclear fusion reaction is: 2 deuterons (each of mass 2.013553 u) → helium-3 nucleus (3.014932 u) + neutron (1.008665 u). Take atomic mass energy conversion u = 931.5 MeV c⁻² and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
items.workedSolution: (a) Δm = Σm_reactants − Σm_products = 3.51 × 10⁻³ u. Final answer: 3.51 × 10⁻³ u. (b) Q = 3.51 × 10⁻³ × 931.5 = 3.27 MeV. Final answer: 3.27 MeV. (c) Total nucleon number A = 4. Final answer: 4.

markScheme.criterion: Sums all reactant and product rest masses including particle multiplicities.
Evaluates correctly to 3.51 × 10⁻³ u.
Multiplies Δm in u by 931.5 MeV u⁻¹.
Evaluates correctly to 3.27 MeV.
Sums nucleon numbers across reactants (or products) to obtain 4.

Assume h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the maximum kinetic energy, in electron-volts (eV), of the emitted photoelectrons?
items.workedSolution: Incident photon energy E = hf / e = (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ × 1.66 × 10¹⁵) / (1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹) = 6.88 eV. Subtracting Φ = 4.08 eV gives Eₖ,ₘₐₓ = 2.80 eV.

markScheme.criterion: Converts hf to eV and subtracts Φ = 4.08 eV to obtain 2.80 eV (D).

items.stem: Measurements from the detector cavern track relativistic kaons in a collider arm cruising at v = 0.9c along a straight spectrometer flight path (proper length L₀ = 27.8 m); in the moving rest frame, the kaon rest-frame proper decay time equals Δt₀ = 1.44 × 10⁻⁸ s. What dilated time interval Δt corresponds to Δt₀ in the stationary observer frame?
items.workedSolution: Lorentz factor γ = 1 / √(1 − 0.9²) = 2.29. Dilated time interval Δt = γ Δt₀ = 2.29 × 1.44 × 10⁻⁸ = 3.30 × 10⁻⁸ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates γ = 2.29 and Δt = γ Δt₀ = 3.30 × 10⁻⁸ s (C).

items.stem: Synchrotron UV radiation filtered to 229 nm illuminates an oxide-free aluminium spacecraft charge-control plate, where the aluminium emitter has Φ = 4.08 eV. Constants: h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, mₑ = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg. What is the maximum speed of the emitted photoelectrons?
items.workedSolution: Incident photon energy E = hc / λ = 8.69 × 10⁻¹⁹ J; work function Φ = 4.08 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 6.53 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. Thus Eₖ,ₘₐₓ = 2.16 × 10⁻¹⁹ J, giving vₘₐₓ = √(2Eₖ,ₘₐₓ / mₑ) = 6.88 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes Eₖ,ₘₐₓ = hc/λ − Φ and vₘₐₓ = √(2Eₖ,ₘₐₓ / mₑ) = 6.88 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: Within a cyclotron-produced PET calibration parent chain, a germanium isotope of nucleon number 68 and proton number 32 decays by purely weak beta-plus transitions (u → d + e⁺ + νₑ) to a nuclide with A = 68 and Z = 30.
items.workedSolution: (a) ΔZ = 30 − 32 = −2. Final answer: −2. (b) N₀ = 68 − 32 = 36; N_f = 68 − 30 = 38. ΔN = N_f − N₀ = 2. Final answer: 2. (c) Accounting for ΔA = 0, charge conservation gives 2 weak beta transitions. Final answer: 2.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Z_final − Z_parent with sign to obtain −2.
Computes N = A − Z for parent and daughter and takes N_final − N_parent.
Evaluates correctly to 2.
Links single-quark flavour conversion to ΔZ = ±1 per weak beta step.
Evaluates correctly to 2.

items.stem: In a heavy-element Coulomb-barrier scattering rig, an energetic proton (charge +1e) with initial kinetic energy 5.1 MeV approaches a stationary lead nucleus (Z = 82, A = 208) directly head-on and recoils elastically. Neglect target recoil and take k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
items.workedSolution: (a) Eₖ = 5.1 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹³ = 8.16 × 10⁻¹³ J. d = k(1e)(82e) / Eₖ = 2.31 × 10⁻¹⁴ m = 23.1 fm. Final answer: 23.1 fm. (b) R = 1.20 × (208)^(1/3) = 7.11 fm (< d, confirming pure electrostatic scattering). Final answer: 7.11 fm. (c) ρ = (208 × 1.661 × 10⁻²⁷) / ((4/3)π(7.11 × 10⁻¹⁵)³) = 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³. Final answer: 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Converts Eₖ to joules, equates Eₖ = k Q₁ Q₂ / d, and converts metres to femtometres.
Evaluates correctly to 23.1 fm.
Applies R = 1.20 × A^(1/3) fm.
Evaluates correctly to 7.11 fm.
Evaluates ρ = A u / ((4/3)πR³) in SI units.
Evaluates correctly to 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³.

items.stem: To verify wave-particle duality, a 2250 V electron beam is directed perpendicularly onto ultrathin polycrystalline platinum foil (d = 2.27 × 10⁻¹⁰ m) at distance L = 0.19 m from a detector screen. Take first-order ring geometry sin θ = λ / d and r = L tan θ, with h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, mₑ = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg, and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
items.workedSolution: (a) p = √(2mₑeV) = 2.56 × 10⁻²³ N s. λ = h / p = 2.59 × 10⁻¹¹ m = 25.9 pm. Final answer: 25.9 pm. (b) sin θ = λ / d = 2.59 × 10⁻¹¹ / (2.27 × 10⁻¹⁰ m) = 0.114. θ = 6.55 °. Final answer: 6.55 °. (c) r = L tan θ = 0.19 × tan(6.55°) = 0.0218 m. Final answer: 0.0218 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses λ = h / √(2mₑeV) with SI values and converts to picometres.
Evaluates correctly to 25.9 pm.
Applies sin θ = λ / d and converts to degrees.
Evaluates correctly to 6.55 °.
Evaluates r = L tan θ using the screen distance L.
Evaluates correctly to 0.0218 m.

items.stem: In a high-mass nuclear density evaluation, alpha particles (Z₁ = 2) of kinetic energy 6.9 MeV scatter from a spherical tungsten-184 target nucleus with proton number Z = 74 and nucleon number A = 184. Model the nuclear radius as R = R₀ A^(1/3) with R₀ = 1.20 fm = 1.20 × 10⁻¹⁵ m and nucleon mass unit u = 1.661 × 10⁻²⁷ kg.
items.workedSolution: (a) R = 1.20 × (184)^(1/3) = 6.83 fm. Final answer: 6.83 fm. (b) R = 6.83 × 10⁻¹⁵ m. Final answer: 6.83 × 10⁻¹⁵ m. (c) m = 184 × 1.661 × 10⁻²⁷ kg; V = (4/3)π(6.83 × 10⁻¹⁵)³. ρ = m / V = 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³. Final answer: 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes nucleon number A into R = R₀ A^(1/3).
Evaluates correctly to 6.83 fm.
Multiplies R in fm by 10⁻¹⁵ m fm⁻¹ to obtain 6.83 × 10⁻¹⁵ m.
Divides nuclear mass A u by spherical volume (4/3)πR³.
Evaluates correctly to 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³.

items.stem: Spectroscopic analysis of argon gas in an inductively coupled argon plasma spectrometer places the ground level at −15.7 eV and a neighbouring bound state at −4.18 eV, taking free electrons at rest to have zero energy. Use h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the longest wavelength of electromagnetic radiation capable of ionizing an atom directly from the ground level?
items.workedSolution: Ionization from the ground level requires ΔE = 0 − (−15.7) = 15.7 eV = 2.51 × 10⁻¹⁸ J. Maximum wavelength λ = hc / ΔE = (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ × 3.00 × 10⁸) / (2.51 × 10⁻¹⁸) = 79.2 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Converts ΔE = 15.7 eV to joules and applies λ = hc / ΔE to obtain 79.2 nm (C).

items.stem: Before testing a fluorine-18 sample (half-life 110 min) in a PET radiopharmacy quality-control well counter, ambient background radiation registers 38 counts min⁻¹. Introducing the source raises the total detector reading to 230 counts min⁻¹ initially, and monitoring continues for an elapsed interval of 220 min. What total count rate (including background) does the detector record at t = 220 min?
items.workedSolution: Initial net count rate C₀ = 230 − 38 = 192 counts min⁻¹. Number of half-lives n = 220 / 110 = 2. Remaining net count rate C = 192 / 2^2 = 48 counts min⁻¹. Total recorded count rate = 48 + 38 = 86.0 counts min⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts background (192), divides by 2^2 (48), and adds 38 back to obtain 86.0 counts min⁻¹ (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides the initial total count rate directly by 2ⁿ without subtracting the background count rate first.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Correctly halves the background-subtracted net count rate but forgets to add the background count rate back to obtain the total detector reading.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Halves the uncorrected count rate first and subtracts the background count rate at the end.

items.stem: In a leukocyte-labelling nuclear medicine lab, a radiochemist prepares 2.4 × 10¹³ radioactive nuclei of indium-111 (half-life T₁/₂ = 2.8 d) and measures the sample again after an elapsed time of 6.1 d. What is the initial activity A₀ of the sample, in Bq, at t = 0?
items.workedSolution: Converting half-life to SI seconds: T₁/₂ = 2.8 × 86400 = 2.42 × 10⁵ s. Decay constant λ = ln 2 / T₁/₂ = 2.87 × 10⁻⁶ s⁻¹. Initial activity A₀ = λN₀ = 6.88 × 10⁷ Bq.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates λ = ln 2 / (2.8 × 86400) and A₀ = λN₀ = 6.88 × 10⁷ Bq (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Leaves T₁/₂ in d instead of converting to seconds when evaluating A₀ = (ln 2 / T₁/₂) N₀ in Bq.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor ln 2 ≈ 0.693 in λ = ln 2 / T₁/₂.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the decayed activity at elapsed time t instead of A₀ at t = 0.

items.stem: Spacetime coordinates (x, ct) in an active galactic nucleus blazar jet model track outer plasma shell S′ boosting at v = 0.56c relative to laboratory S while faster inner shock front propagates collinearly at u = 0.87c in S. What is the dimensionless velocity ratio u′ / c of faster inner shock front measured in frame S′?

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes u and v with signs into u′/c = (u/c − v/c) / (1 − uv/c²) = 0.605 (B).

items.stem: Spectra recorded from an X-ray binary accretion-disc corona show five-times ionized carbon C⁵⁺ (Z = 6) whose bound levels follow Eₙ = −13.6 Z² / n² eV relative to the ionization continuum. Consider ions prepared in excited shell n = 3 (with h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C).
items.workedSolution: (a) Eₙ = −13.6 × (6)² / (3)² = −54.4 eV. Ionization energy ΔE = 0 − Eₙ = 54.4 eV. Final answer: 54.4 eV. (b) ΔE = 54.4 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 8.70 × 10⁻¹⁸ J. f = ΔE / h = 8.70 × 10⁻¹⁸ / (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴) = 1.31 × 10¹⁶ Hz. Final answer: 1.31 × 10¹⁶ Hz. (c) λ = (3.00 × 10⁸) / (1.31 × 10¹⁶) = 22.9 nm. Final answer: 22.9 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Applies ΔE = 13.6 Z² / n² eV for the specified Z and n.
Evaluates correctly to 54.4 eV.
Converts ionization energy from eV to J and divides by Planck's constant h.
Evaluates correctly to 1.31 × 10¹⁶ Hz.
Uses λ = c / f and expresses the wavelength in nm to obtain 22.9 nm.

items.workedSolution: (a) Eₖ = qV = 5.76 × 10⁻¹⁶ J. v = √(2Eₖ / m) = 4.16 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹. Final answer: 4.16 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹. (b) λ = h / (mv) = 2.40 × 10⁻¹³ m = 2.40 × 10⁻⁴ nm. Final answer: 2.40 × 10⁻⁴ nm. (c) λ = 0.240 pm. Final answer: 0.240 pm.

markScheme.criterion: Equates ½mv² = qV and solves v = √(2qV / m).
Evaluates correctly to 4.16 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹.
Divides Planck's constant h by mv and converts metres to nanometres.
Evaluates correctly to 2.40 × 10⁻⁴ nm.
Multiplies wavelength in nm by 1000 pm nm⁻¹ to obtain 0.240 pm.

items.stem: Energy-balance modelling of a magnetic-confinement tokamak D–T plasma burn considers deuterium–tritium fusion: deuteron (A = 2, Z = 1, mass 2.013553 u) + triton (A = 3, Z = 1, mass 3.015501 u) → helium nucleus (A = 4, Z = 2, mass 4.001506 u) + neutron (mass 1.008665 u). Use u = 931.5 MeV c⁻² and elementary charge e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. How much nuclear energy Q, in MeV, is released in one fusion event?
items.workedSolution: Mass decrease Δm = Σm_reactants − Σm_products = 0.0189 u. Energy released Q = Δm × 931.5 = 17.6 MeV.

markScheme.criterion: Computes Δm = 0.0189 u and Q = Δm × 931.5 = 17.6 MeV (A).

items.stem: To calibrate a solar-blind magnesium UV flame-sensor cathode, ultraviolet photons at 1.62 × 10¹⁵ Hz irradiate a magnesium electrode having Φ = 3.66 eV. Constants: h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
items.workedSolution: (a) Φ = 3.66 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 5.86 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. f₀ = Φ / h = 5.86 × 10⁻¹⁹ / (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴) = 8.83 × 10¹⁴ Hz. Final answer: 8.83 × 10¹⁴ Hz. (b) Photon energy E = hf / e = 6.71 eV. Eₖ,ₘₐₓ = 6.71 − 3.66 = 3.05 eV. Final answer: 3.05 eV. (c) Vₛ = Eₖ,ₘₐₓ / e = 3.05 V. Final answer: 3.05 V.

markScheme.criterion: Converts Φ from eV to joules and applies f₀ = Φ / h.
Evaluates correctly to 8.83 × 10¹⁴ Hz.
Applies Einstein's photoelectric equation Eₖ,ₘₐₓ = hf/e − Φ.
Evaluates correctly to 3.05 eV.
Uses eVₛ = Eₖ,ₘₐₓ to obtain 3.05 V.

items.stem: In a fuel-cladding activation beta-minus sequence, a parent zirconium nucleus (A = 95, Z = 40) transforms via purely weak beta-minus transitions (d → u + e⁻ + ν̄ₑ) into a final nuclide with A = 95 and Z = 42, conserving baryon and lepton numbers at every vertex. What is the signed net change in neutron number ΔN = N_final − N_parent across the sequence?
items.workedSolution: Initial neutron number N₀ = 95 − 40 = 55; final neutron number N_f = 95 − 42 = 53. Thus ΔN = N_f − N₀ = −2.

markScheme.criterion: Uses N = A − Z to obtain ΔN = (95 − 42) − (95 − 40) = −2 (A).

items.stem: Elastic 180° backscattering in a refractory-foil elastic alpha-scattering chamber sends a 4.2 MeV alpha particle (charge +2e) directly toward an immobile tungsten target nucleus (Z = 74, A = 184), taking k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the distance of closest approach d, in femtometres (fm)?
items.workedSolution: Initial kinetic energy Eₖ = 4.2 × 10⁶ × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 6.72 × 10⁻¹³ J. At the turning point, Eₖ = k(2e)(74e) / d, so d = (8.99 × 10⁹)(2)(74)(1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹)² / 6.72 × 10⁻¹³ = 50.7 fm.

markScheme.criterion: Equates Eₖ to k Q₁ Q₂ / d to obtain d = 50.7 fm (B).

items.stem: Within a targeted alpha-immunotherapy generator column, heavy actinium nuclei of mass number 227 and atomic number 89 undergo alpha and beta-minus steps to reach A = 211, Z = 83. What is the net change in neutron number ΔN = N_final − N_parent across the entire chain?
items.workedSolution: Parent neutron number N₀ = 227 − 89 = 138. Final neutron number N_f = 211 − 83 = 128. Therefore ΔN = N_f − N₀ = −10.

items.stem: Within a Thomson-type diffraction bulb, 320 V electrons traverse thin polycrystalline nickel foil whose crystal planes are separated by d = 2.03 × 10⁻¹⁰ m, illuminating a ring on a screen L = 0.18 m away (sin θ = λ / d, r = L tan θ, h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, mₑ = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C). What is the first-order diffraction angle θ, in degrees?
items.workedSolution: Electron wavelength λ = h / √(2mₑeV) = 6.86 × 10⁻¹¹ m. Using sin θ = λ / d = 0.338 yields θ = arcsin(0.338) = 19.8 °.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates λ = h / √(2mₑeV) and θ = arcsin(λ / d) = 19.8 ° (D).

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inserts an extra factor of 2 in the denominator despite sin θ = λ / d being specified.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 in p = √(2mₑeV) when computing the electron de Broglie wavelength.

items.stem: During a charge-distribution scattering experiment, a 5.2 MeV alpha beam (charge +2e) probes calcium-40 nuclei (Z = 20, A = 40). Assume a uniform spherical nucleus obeying R = R₀ A^(1/3), where R₀ = 1.20 fm = 1.20 × 10⁻¹⁵ m and u = 1.661 × 10⁻²⁷ kg. Assuming nuclear mass m ≈ A u, what is the nuclear matter density ρ of this calcium-40 nucleus?
items.workedSolution: Since R = R₀ A^(1/3), V = (4/3)πR³ = (4/3)π R₀³ A. Thus ρ = (A u) / ((4/3)π R₀³ A) = 3u / (4π R₀³) = 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Computes ρ = A u / ((4/3)πR³) = 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³ (C).

items.stem: The energy-level diagram illustrates radiative transitions in helium gas within a stellar chromosphere helium absorption cell. An atom initially occupies the second excited state at energy −3.39 eV (with a nearby level at −4.8 eV and ionization at zero eV). Take h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
items.workedSolution: (a) ΔE = 0 − (−3.39) = 3.39 eV. Final answer: 3.39 eV. (b) ΔE = 3.39 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 5.42 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. f = ΔE / h = 5.42 × 10⁻¹⁹ / (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴) = 8.18 × 10¹⁴ Hz. Final answer: 8.18 × 10¹⁴ Hz. (c) λ = c / f = (3.00 × 10⁸) / (8.18 × 10¹⁴) = 3.67 × 10⁻⁷ m. Converting to nanometres gives λ = 367 nm. Final answer: 367 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Finds ΔE = 0 − E_initial in eV to obtain 3.39 eV.
Converts ΔE to joules (× 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹) and applies f = ΔE / h.
Evaluates correctly to 8.18 × 10¹⁴ Hz.
Uses λ = c / f (or hc / ΔE) and converts metres to nanometres.
Evaluates correctly to 367 nm.

items.stem: A radiation detector in an environmental air-filter beta counter operates in a steady background of 26 counts min⁻¹. A fresh bismuth-214 specimen with half-life 19.9 min gives an initial uncorrected reading of 306 counts min⁻¹. Consider the detector response after 59.7 min.
items.workedSolution: (a) C₀,net = 306 − 26 = 280 counts min⁻¹. Final answer: 280 counts min⁻¹. (b) n = 59.7 / 19.9 = 3 half-lives. C_net = 280 / 2^3 = 35.0 counts min⁻¹. Final answer: 35.0 counts min⁻¹. (c) C_total = 34.99999999999999 + 26 = 61.0 counts min⁻¹. Final answer: 61.0 counts min⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts background count rate from initial total count rate to obtain 280 counts min⁻¹.
Identifies 3 elapsed half-lives and divides initial net count rate by 2^3.
Evaluates correctly to 35.0 counts min⁻¹.
Adds background count rate back to the remaining net count rate to obtain 61.0 counts min⁻¹.

parts.prompt: Determine the initial corrected count rate due solely to the bismuth-214 source at t = 0.
Calculate the corrected count rate from the source alone at t = 59.7 min.
State the total count rate displayed by the detector at t = 59.7 min.

items.stem: Quality-assurance logs in a weld-inspection gamma radiography vault record an initial population of 3.7 × 10¹³ iridium-192 nuclei with half-life 73.8 d. Consider the source after 101 d of continuous exponential decay.

markScheme.criterion: Converts T₁/₂ from d to seconds and applies λ = ln 2 / T₁/₂.
Evaluates correctly to 1.09 × 10⁻⁷ s⁻¹.
Multiplies λ in s⁻¹ by N₀ using A₀ = λN₀.
Evaluates correctly to 4.02 × 10⁶ Bq.
Applies exponential decay law A = A₀ e^(−λt) with consistent time units.
Evaluates correctly to 1.56 × 10⁶ Bq.

Determine the activity A of the sample, in Bq, after t = 101 d.

items.stem: Within a laser-produced ablation plasma plume, one-electron four-times ionized boron B⁴⁺ (Z = 5) ions populate principal shell n = 1 under the Bohr scaling law Eₙ = −13.6 Z² / n² eV relative to zero continuum energy (h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C). What minimum photon frequency is needed to remove the electron completely from principal shell n = 1?
items.workedSolution: Ionization energy from n = 1 is ΔE = 13.6 × 5² / 1² = 340 eV = 5.44 × 10⁻¹⁷ J. Threshold frequency f = ΔE / h = 8.21 × 10¹⁶ Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates f = (13.6 Z² / n²)(e / h) = 8.21 × 10¹⁶ Hz (D).

items.stem: Evaluating strong-force binding in a liquid-metal fast-reactor coolant data sheet, a fully stripped sodium-23 nucleus (proton number Z = 11, nucleon number A = 23) has rest mass 22.983733 u. Constants: mₚ = 1.007276 u, mₙ = 1.008665 u, u = 931.5 MeV c⁻². What is the binding energy per nucleon, in MeV, of this sodium-23 nucleus?
items.workedSolution: Neutron count N = 23 − 11 = 12. Mass defect Δm = 11(1.007276) + 12(1.008665) − 22.983733 = 0.200 u. Total binding energy B = Δm × 931.5 = 187 MeV. Binding energy per nucleon B / A = 187 / 23 = 8.11 MeV.

markScheme.criterion: Computes Δm = 0.200 u, B = 187 MeV, and B / A = 8.11 MeV (D).

items.stem: In a low-energy electron diffraction (LEED) gun, a collimated stream of electrons is accelerated from rest by a 4200 V supply. Constants: h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, mₑ = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the de Broglie wavelength, in picometres (pm), of the electrons?
items.workedSolution: Kinetic energy Eₖ = qV = 6.72 × 10⁻¹⁶ J. Momentum p = √(2mEₖ) = 3.50 × 10⁻²³ N s. De Broglie wavelength λ = h / p = 18.9 pm.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates p and λ = h / p to obtain 18.9 pm (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 inside p = √(2mEₖ), computing λ = h / √(mEₖ).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the elementary charge factor e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C when converting accelerating voltage to joules.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Treats the massive particle as a massless photon using λ = hc / E instead of λ = h / p.

items.stem: Reaction kinematics in a linear-accelerator proton–lithium target experiment examine proton–lithium-7 Cockcroft–Walton fusion, where bare rest masses satisfy proton (1.007276 u) + lithium-7 nucleus (7.014358 u) → 2 alpha particles (each of mass 4.001506 u). Assume 1 u = 931.5 MeV c⁻² and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
items.workedSolution: (a) Δm = Σm_reactants − Σm_products = 0.0186 u. Final answer: 0.0186 u. (b) Q = 0.0186 × 931.5 = 17.3 MeV. Final answer: 17.3 MeV. (c) Total nucleon number A = 8. Final answer: 8.

markScheme.criterion: Sums all reactant and product rest masses including particle multiplicities.
Evaluates correctly to 0.0186 u.
Multiplies Δm in u by 931.5 MeV u⁻¹.
Evaluates correctly to 17.3 MeV.
Sums nucleon numbers across reactants (or products) to obtain 8.

items.stem: Monochromatic electromagnetic radiation of frequency 2.87 × 10¹⁵ Hz strikes an oxygen-free copper accelerator photocathode whose work function is 4.7 eV. Take h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the maximum kinetic energy, in electron-volts (eV), of the emitted photoelectrons?
items.workedSolution: Incident photon energy E = hf / e = (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ × 2.87 × 10¹⁵) / (1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹) = 11.9 eV. Subtracting Φ = 4.7 eV gives Eₖ,ₘₐₓ = 7.19 eV.

markScheme.criterion: Converts hf to eV and subtracts Φ = 4.7 eV to obtain 7.19 eV (A).

What is the Lorentz factor γ for this relative speed v = 0.6c?

items.stem: Monochromatic photons of wavelength 208 nm eject photoelectrons in vacuum from a degassed calcium photoemission electrode (calcium, Φ = 2.87 eV). Assume h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, and mₑ = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg. What is the maximum speed of the emitted photoelectrons?
items.workedSolution: Incident photon energy E = hc / λ = 9.56 × 10⁻¹⁹ J; work function Φ = 2.87 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 4.59 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. Thus Eₖ,ₘₐₓ = 4.97 × 10⁻¹⁹ J, giving vₘₐₓ = √(2Eₖ,ₘₐₓ / mₑ) = 1.04 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes Eₖ,ₘₐₓ = hc/λ − Φ and vₘₐₓ = √(2Eₖ,ₘₐₓ / mₑ) = 1.04 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Particle-nuclear tracking in a proton-beam spallation iron-52 decay chain follows a iron parent (nucleon number 52, proton number 26) undergoing purely weak beta-plus transitions (u → d + e⁺ + νₑ) to form a daughter nucleus (A = 52, Z = 24).
items.workedSolution: (a) ΔZ = 24 − 26 = −2. Final answer: −2. (b) N₀ = 52 − 26 = 26; N_f = 52 − 24 = 28. ΔN = N_f − N₀ = 2. Final answer: 2. (c) Accounting for ΔA = 0, charge conservation gives 2 weak beta transitions. Final answer: 2.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Z_final − Z_parent with sign to obtain −2.
Computes N = A − Z for parent and daughter and takes N_final − N_parent.
Evaluates correctly to 2.
Links single-quark flavour conversion to ΔZ = ±1 per weak beta step.
Evaluates correctly to 2.

items.stem: During an experiment in a heavy-element Coulomb-barrier scattering rig, an alpha particle (charge +2e) of kinetic energy 3.6 MeV is directed along a head-on trajectory toward a fixed lead nucleus (proton number Z = 82, nucleon number A = 208). Use k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
items.workedSolution: (a) Eₖ = 3.6 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹³ = 5.76 × 10⁻¹³ J. d = k(2e)(82e) / Eₖ = 6.55 × 10⁻¹⁴ m = 65.5 fm. Final answer: 65.5 fm. (b) R = 1.20 × (208)^(1/3) = 7.11 fm (< d, confirming pure electrostatic scattering). Final answer: 7.11 fm. (c) ρ = (208 × 1.661 × 10⁻²⁷) / ((4/3)π(7.11 × 10⁻¹⁵)³) = 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³. Final answer: 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Converts Eₖ to joules, equates Eₖ = k Q₁ Q₂ / d, and converts metres to femtometres.
Evaluates correctly to 65.5 fm.
Applies R = 1.20 × A^(1/3) fm.
Evaluates correctly to 7.11 fm.
Evaluates ρ = A u / ((4/3)πR³) in SI units.
Evaluates correctly to 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³.

items.stem: In an evacuated electron-diffraction tube, electrons accelerated from rest through 1300 V pass through sputtered polycrystalline silver film of interplanar spacing d = 2.36 × 10⁻¹⁰ m and form concentric bright rings on a phosphor screen L = 0.17 m behind the foil. Use sin θ = λ / d and ring radius r = L tan θ, taking h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, mₑ = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg, and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
items.workedSolution: (a) p = √(2mₑeV) = 1.95 × 10⁻²³ N s. λ = h / p = 3.41 × 10⁻¹¹ m = 34.1 pm. Final answer: 34.1 pm. (b) sin θ = λ / d = 3.41 × 10⁻¹¹ / (2.36 × 10⁻¹⁰ m) = 0.144. θ = 8.30 °. Final answer: 8.30 °. (c) r = L tan θ = 0.17 × tan(8.30°) = 0.0248 m. Final answer: 0.0248 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses λ = h / √(2mₑeV) with SI values and converts to picometres.
Evaluates correctly to 34.1 pm.
Applies sin θ = λ / d and converts to degrees.
Evaluates correctly to 8.30 °.
Evaluates r = L tan θ using the screen distance L.
Evaluates correctly to 0.0248 m.

items.stem: In a closed-proton-shell tin scattering run, alpha particles (Z₁ = 2) of kinetic energy 6.5 MeV scatter from a spherical tin-120 target nucleus with proton number Z = 50 and nucleon number A = 120. items.workedSolution: (a) R = 1.20 × (120)^(1/3) = 5.92 fm. Final answer: 5.92 fm. (b) R = 5.92 × 10⁻¹⁵ m. Final answer: 5.92 × 10⁻¹⁵ m. (c) m = 120 × 1.661 × 10⁻²⁷ kg; V = (4/3)π(5.92 × 10⁻¹⁵)³. ρ = m / V = 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³. Final answer: 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³.

items.stem: A vapour cell in a laser-cooled rubidium magnetometry cell contains rubidium vapour whose the first excited state lies at −2.63 eV and whose adjacent bound level lies at −4.27 eV relative to the continuum threshold. Assume h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What minimum photon frequency is required to ionize the atom from the first excited state?
items.workedSolution: Energy needed to reach the continuum is ΔE = 2.63 eV = 4.21 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. Threshold frequency f = ΔE / h = 4.21 × 10⁻¹⁹ / (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴) = 6.35 × 10¹⁴ Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Uses f = |E| e / h to obtain 6.35 × 10¹⁴ Hz (D).

items.stem: At a hospital nuclear-medicine dispenser, a Geiger–Müller tube measures a mean background count rate of 18 counts min⁻¹ with no sample present. When a technetium-99m source of half-life 6 h is placed in front of the window at t = 0, the total recorded count rate is 118 counts min⁻¹. The detector is read again at t = 12 h. What total count rate (including background) does the detector record at t = 12 h?
items.workedSolution: Initial net count rate C₀ = 118 − 18 = 100 counts min⁻¹. Number of half-lives n = 12 / 6 = 2. Remaining net count rate C = 100 / 2^2 = 25 counts min⁻¹. Total recorded count rate = 25 + 18 = 43.0 counts min⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts background (100), divides by 2^2 (25), and adds 18 back to obtain 43.0 counts min⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides the initial total count rate directly by 2ⁿ without subtracting the background count rate first.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Correctly halves the background-subtracted net count rate but forgets to add the background count rate back to obtain the total detector reading.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Halves the uncorrected count rate first and subtracts the background count rate at the end.

items.stem: A freshly prepared vial in a weld-inspection gamma radiography vault contains N₀ = 4.3 × 10¹⁵ undecayed nuclei of iridium-192, whose half-life is 73.8 d. The vial is stored for t = 120 d before administration. What is the activity of the sample, in becquerels (Bq), at t = 120 d?
items.workedSolution: T₁/₂ = 73.8 × 86400 = 6.38 × 10⁶ s, so λ = ln 2 / T₁/₂ = 1.09 × 10⁻⁷ s⁻¹. Initial activity A₀ = λN₀ = 4.67 × 10⁸ Bq. At t = 120 d, A = A₀ e^(−λt) = 1.51 × 10⁸ Bq.

markScheme.criterion: Converts T₁/₂ to seconds, finds A₀ = λN₀, and evaluates A = A₀ e^(−λt) = 1.51 × 10⁸ Bq (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Fails to convert half-life from d to seconds (× 86400) when computing A = λN in Bq (s⁻¹).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the initial activity A₀ = λN₀ at t = 0 without multiplying by the exponential decay factor e^(−λt).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses λ = 1 / T₁/₂ instead of λ = ln 2 / T₁/₂ when converting half-life to decay constant.

items.stem: Relativistic kinematics in an orbital optical-clock Doppler link relates rest frame S to moving frame S′ (outbound relay platform S′) boosted at v = 0.4c along +x. In frame S, inbound return transponder has velocity component u = −0.66c. What is the dimensionless velocity ratio u′ / c of inbound return transponder measured in frame S′?

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes u and v with signs into u′/c = (u/c − v/c) / (1 − uv/c²) = −0.839 (A).

items.stem: Radiative recombination diagnostics on an electron-beam ion-trap (EBIT) X-ray source analyse single-electron beryllium Be³⁺ (Z = 4) starting from outer bound shell n = 5 using Eₙ = −13.6 Z² / n² eV. Assume h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
items.workedSolution: (a) Eₙ = −13.6 × (4)² / (5)² = −8.70 eV. Ionization energy ΔE = 0 − Eₙ = 8.70 eV. Final answer: 8.70 eV. (b) ΔE = 8.70 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 1.39 × 10⁻¹⁸ J. f = ΔE / h = 1.39 × 10⁻¹⁸ / (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴) = 2.10 × 10¹⁵ Hz. Final answer: 2.10 × 10¹⁵ Hz. (c) λ = (3.00 × 10⁸) / (2.10 × 10¹⁵) = 143 nm. Final answer: 143 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Applies ΔE = 13.6 Z² / n² eV for the specified Z and n.
Evaluates correctly to 8.70 eV.
Converts ionization energy from eV to J and divides by Planck's constant h.
Evaluates correctly to 2.10 × 10¹⁵ Hz.
Uses λ = c / f and expresses the wavelength in nm to obtain 143 nm.

parts.prompt: Calculate the ionization energy, in eV, required to remove the electron from outer bound shell n = 5.
Determine the threshold ionizing photon frequency.
Calculate the maximum photon wavelength, in nm, capable of ionizing this state.

items.stem: Precision ion-trap records from a neutron-capture control-rod mass evaluation report a bare boron-10 nuclear mass of 10.010194 u for A = 10 and Z = 5. Take mₚ = 1.007276 u, mₙ = 1.008665 u, and 1 u = 931.5 MeV c⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Finds N = A − Z and evaluates Δm = Z mₚ + N mₙ − m_nuc.
Evaluates correctly to 0.0695 u.
Multiplies mass defect Δm in u by 931.5 MeV u⁻¹.

items.stem: Reaction kinematics in a mixed-oxide thermal reactor assembly examine molybdenum–tin fission of plutonium-239, where bare rest masses satisfy plutonium nucleus (239.0006 u) + 1 thermal neutron (1.008665 u) → tin-134 nucleus (133.8902 u) + ruthenium-103 nucleus (102.8825 u) + 3 neutrons (each 1.008665 u). Eₖ,ₘₐₓ = 10.4 − 4.33 = 6.03 eV. Final answer: 6.03 eV. (c) Vₛ = Eₖ,ₘₐₓ / e = 6.03 V. Final answer: 6.03 V.
