items.stem: Electrostatic repulsion inside a heavy-metal beam-diagnostics scattering foil halts a head-on proton (charge +1e) of initial energy 5.1 MeV at closest approach d from a stationary tantalum nucleus (Z = 73, A = 181). Assume k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the distance of closest approach d, in femtometres (fm)?
items.workedSolution: Initial kinetic energy Eₖ = 5.1 × 10⁶ × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 8.16 × 10⁻¹³ J. At the turning point, Eₖ = k(1e)(73e) / d, so d = (8.99 × 10⁹)(1)(73)(1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹)² / 8.16 × 10⁻¹³ = 20.6 fm.

markScheme.criterion: Equates Eₖ to k Q₁ Q₂ / d to obtain d = 20.6 fm (D).

items.stem: Nuclear stability mapping of an alpha-proton X-ray spectrometer source connects parent curium (A = 244, Z = 96) to product nuclide (A = 228, Z = 90) through a series consisting strictly of alpha and beta-minus emissions. How many beta-minus particles are emitted in this decay sequence?
items.workedSolution: Only alpha decay changes nucleon number A: Nα = (244 − 228) / 4 = 4. Proton balance gives 90 = 96 − 2(4) + Nβ⁻, so Nβ⁻ = 90 − 88 = 2.

markScheme.criterion: Finds Nα = 4 from ΔA / 4 and solves Z_f = Z_0 − 2Nα + Nβ⁻ to obtain Nβ⁻ = 2 (D).

options.distractorRationale: Assigns ΔZ = −1 instead of ΔZ = +1 to beta-minus decay when solving the proton-number balance.

items.stem: Electrons accelerated from rest by a 4450 V supply diffract through evaporated polycrystalline gold film with lattice spacing d = 2.35 × 10⁻¹⁰ m, producing a circular first-order ring on a screen at distance L = 0.15 m. Given sin θ = λ / d, r = L tan θ, h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, mₑ = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg, and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C: What is the radius r of the first-order bright diffraction ring on the screen?
items.workedSolution: λ = h / √(2mₑeV) = 1.84 × 10⁻¹¹ m. Then sin θ = λ / d = 0.0783, giving θ = 4.49 ° and ring radius r = L tan θ = 0.15 × tan(4.49°) = 0.0118 m.

markScheme.criterion: Finds λ = 1.84 × 10⁻¹¹ m, θ = 4.49°, and r = L tan θ = 0.0118 m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the full diameter 2r of the diffraction ring instead of its radius r.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 inside p = √(2mₑeV), overestimating λ and ring radius by √2.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the diffraction ratio as d / λ instead of λ / d.

items.stem: Within a medium-light nuclear size determination, 5.6 MeV helium-4 nuclei (Z₁ = 2) scatter elastically off sulfur-32 (Z = 16, A = 32). Model the target as a uniform sphere of radius R = R₀ A^(1/3) with R₀ = 1.20 fm = 1.20 × 10⁻¹⁵ m and u = 1.661 × 10⁻²⁷ kg. What is the estimated nuclear radius R, in femtometres (fm), of the sulfur-32 nucleus?

items.stem: Spectroscopic analysis of rubidium vapour in a laser-cooled rubidium magnetometry cell places the first excited state at −2.59 eV and a neighbouring bound state at −4.18 eV, taking free electrons at rest to have zero energy. Use h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
items.workedSolution: (a) ΔE = 0 − (−2.59) = 2.59 eV. Final answer: 2.59 eV. (b) ΔE = 2.59 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 4.14 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. f = ΔE / h = 4.14 × 10⁻¹⁹ / (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴) = 6.25 × 10¹⁴ Hz. Final answer: 6.25 × 10¹⁴ Hz. (c) λ = c / f = (3.00 × 10⁸) / (6.25 × 10¹⁴) = 4.80 × 10⁻⁷ m. Converting to nanometres gives λ = 480 nm. Final answer: 480 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Finds ΔE = 0 − E_initial in eV to obtain 2.59 eV.
Converts ΔE to joules (× 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹) and applies f = ΔE / h.
Evaluates correctly to 6.25 × 10¹⁴ Hz.
Uses λ = c / f (or hc / ΔE) and converts metres to nanometres.
Evaluates correctly to 480 nm.

items.stem: At a positron-imaging elution calibrator, a Geiger–Müller tube measures a mean background count rate of 18 counts min⁻¹ with no sample present. When a gallium-68 source of half-life 68 min is placed in front of the window at t = 0, the total recorded count rate is 418 counts min⁻¹. The detector is read again at t = 272 min.
items.workedSolution: (a) C₀,net = 418 − 18 = 400 counts min⁻¹. Final answer: 400 counts min⁻¹. (b) n = 272 / 68 = 4 half-lives. C_net = 400 / 2^4 = 25.0 counts min⁻¹. Final answer: 25.0 counts min⁻¹. (c) C_total = 25 + 18 = 43.0 counts min⁻¹. Final answer: 43.0 counts min⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts background count rate from initial total count rate to obtain 400 counts min⁻¹.
Identifies 4 elapsed half-lives and divides initial net count rate by 2^4.
Evaluates correctly to 25.0 counts min⁻¹.
Adds background count rate back to the remaining net count rate to obtain 43.0 counts min⁻¹.

parts.prompt: Determine the initial corrected count rate due solely to the gallium-68 source at t = 0.
Calculate the corrected count rate from the source alone at t = 272 min.
State the total count rate displayed by the detector at t = 272 min.

markScheme.criterion: Converts T₁/₂ from min to seconds and applies λ = ln 2 / T₁/₂.

Multiplies λ in s⁻¹ by N₀ using A₀ = λN₀.
Evaluates correctly to 7.77 × 10¹⁰ Bq.
Applies exponential decay law A = A₀ e^(−λt) with consistent time units.
Evaluates correctly to 1.10 × 10¹⁰ Bq.

items.stem: Radiative recombination diagnostics on an electron-beam ion-trap (EBIT) X-ray source analyse single-electron beryllium Be³⁺ (Z = 4) starting from outer bound shell n = 5 using Eₙ = −13.6 Z² / n² eV. Assume h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the series-limit (maximum) photon wavelength that can photoionize this species from outer bound shell n = 5?
items.workedSolution: Initial level energy Eₙ = −13.6 × 4² / 5² = −8.70 eV. Ionization requires ΔE = 8.70 eV = 1.39 × 10⁻¹⁸ J. Maximum ionizing wavelength λ = hc / ΔE = 143 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Computes ΔE = 13.6 Z² / n² eV and λ = hc / ΔE = 143 nm (B).

items.stem: To benchmark nuclear stability in a supernova core stability-peak measurement, consider a bare iron-56 nucleus of nucleon number A = 56, proton number Z = 26, and nuclear mass 55.920674 u (mₚ = 1.007276 u, mₙ = 1.008665 u, u = 931.5 MeV c⁻²). What is the binding energy per nucleon, in MeV, of this iron-56 nucleus?
items.workedSolution: Neutron count N = 56 − 26 = 30. Mass defect Δm = 26(1.007276) + 30(1.008665) − 55.920674 = 0.528 u. Total binding energy B = Δm × 931.5 = 492 MeV. Binding energy per nucleon B / A = 492 / 56 = 8.79 MeV.

markScheme.criterion: Computes Δm = 0.528 u, B = 492 MeV, and B / A = 8.79 MeV (A).

items.stem: A beam of protons starts from rest in a surface-analysis proton microprobe injector and accelerates through a potential difference of 220 V in vacuum. Take h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, mₚ = 1.673 × 10⁻²⁷ kg, and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the de Broglie wavelength, in picometres (pm), of the protons?
items.workedSolution: Kinetic energy Eₖ = qV = 3.52 × 10⁻¹⁷ J. Momentum p = √(2mEₖ) = 3.43 × 10⁻²² N s. De Broglie wavelength λ = h / p = 1.93 pm.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates p and λ = h / p to obtain 1.93 pm (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 inside p = √(2mEₖ), computing λ = h / √(mEₖ).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the elementary charge factor e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C when converting accelerating voltage to joules.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats the massive particle as a massless photon using λ = hc / E instead of λ = h / p.

items.stem: Energy-balance modelling of an electrostatic-confinement D–³He fusion chamber considers deuterium–helium-3 aneutronic fusion: deuteron (2.013553 u) + helium-3 nucleus (3.014932 u) → alpha particle (4.001506 u) + proton (1.007276 u). Use u = 931.5 MeV c⁻² and elementary charge e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
items.workedSolution: (a) Δm = Σm_reactants − Σm_products = 0.0197 u. Final answer: 0.0197 u. (b) Q = 0.0197 × 931.5 = 18.4 MeV. Final answer: 18.4 MeV. (c) Total nucleon number A = 5. Final answer: 5.

markScheme.criterion: Sums all reactant and product rest masses including particle multiplicities.
Evaluates correctly to 0.0197 u.
Multiplies Δm in u by 931.5 MeV u⁻¹.
Evaluates correctly to 18.4 MeV.
Sums nucleon numbers across reactants (or products) to obtain 5.

Take h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What reverse stopping potential Vₛ is required to reduce the collector photocurrent to zero?
items.workedSolution: Photon energy E = hf / e = (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ × 6.16 × 10¹⁴) / (1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹) = 2.55 eV. Maximum kinetic energy Eₖ,ₘₐₓ = E − Φ = 2.55 − 1.95 = 0.603 eV. Hence stopping potential Vₛ = 0.603 V.

markScheme.criterion: Computes eVₛ = hf − Φ to obtain Vₛ = 0.603 V (D).

items.stem: Within two stationary relay towers, a deep-space relativistic courier vessel maintain speed v = 0.84c across the inter-beacon corridor whose proper length is L₀ = 5.04 × 10⁹ m; their onboard telemetry cycle duration is Δt₀ = 19.6 s. What contracted length L of the baseline L₀ is measured in the moving rest frame?
items.workedSolution: Lorentz factor γ = 1 / √(1 − 0.84²) = 1.84. Contracted length L = L₀ / γ = 5.04 × 10⁹ / 1.84 = 2.73 × 10⁹ m.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates γ = 1.84 and L = L₀ / γ = 2.73 × 10⁹ m (A).

items.stem: An excimer UV laser operating at wavelength 148 nm irradiates a freshly cleaved lithium vacuum target (lithium work function 2.93 eV). Take h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, and mₑ = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg. What is the maximum speed of the emitted photoelectrons?
items.workedSolution: Incident photon energy E = hc / λ = 1.34 × 10⁻¹⁸ J; work function Φ = 2.93 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 4.69 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. Thus Eₖ,ₘₐₓ = 8.75 × 10⁻¹⁹ J, giving vₘₐₓ = √(2Eₖ,ₘₐₓ / mₑ) = 1.39 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes Eₖ,ₘₐₓ = hc/λ − Φ and vₘₐₓ = √(2Eₖ,ₘₐₓ / mₑ) = 1.39 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: Standard-Model weak-interaction analysis of a mass-141 fission-fragment isobaric decay chain links parent barium (A = 141, Z = 56) to daughter (A = 141, Z = 59) through purely weak beta-minus transitions (d → u + e⁻ + ν̄ₑ). How many individual quark-level d → u weak beta transitions occur between the parent and final nucleus?
items.workedSolution: Each weak beta step flips exactly one quark inside a nucleon, changing Z by +1 while keeping A constant. Accounting for ΔA = 0 gives 3 weak quark transitions.

markScheme.criterion: Balances A and Z to identify 3 single-quark weak beta transitions (D).

items.stem: A collimated alpha particle (charge +2e) carrying 4.5 MeV of kinetic energy undergoes direct head-on Coulomb backscattering from a stationary palladium nucleus (Z = 46, A = 106) inside a high-vacuum elastic backscattering stage. Constants: k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻², e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the distance of closest approach d, in femtometres (fm)?
items.workedSolution: Initial kinetic energy Eₖ = 4.5 × 10⁶ × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 7.20 × 10⁻¹³ J. At the turning point, Eₖ = k(2e)(46e) / d, so d = (8.99 × 10⁹)(2)(46)(1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹)² / 7.20 × 10⁻¹³ = 29.4 fm.

markScheme.criterion: Equates Eₖ to k Q₁ Q₂ / d to obtain d = 29.4 fm (D).

items.stem: A multi-step nuclear decay series in a pitchblende ore core sample transforms a parent radium nucleus (nucleon number 226, proton number 88) exclusively via alpha and beta-minus transitions into a final nuclide with nucleon number 206 and proton number 80. What is the net change in neutron number ΔN = N_final − N_parent across the entire chain?
items.workedSolution: Parent neutron number N₀ = 226 − 88 = 138. Final neutron number N_f = 206 − 80 = 126. Therefore ΔN = N_f − N₀ = −12.

items.stem: Electrons accelerated from rest by a 980 V supply diffract through evaporated polycrystalline gold film with lattice spacing d = 2.35 × 10⁻¹⁰ m, producing a circular first-order ring on a screen at distance L = 0.15 m. Given sin θ = λ / d, r = L tan θ, h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, mₑ = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg, and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C: What is the first-order diffraction angle θ, in degrees?
items.workedSolution: Electron wavelength λ = h / √(2mₑeV) = 3.92 × 10⁻¹¹ m. Using sin θ = λ / d = 0.167 yields θ = arcsin(0.167) = 9.61 °.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates λ = h / √(2mₑeV) and θ = arcsin(λ / d) = 9.61 ° (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Leaves arcsin(λ / d) in radians while labelling the answer in degrees.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inserts an extra factor of 2 in the denominator despite sin θ = λ / d being specified.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 in p = √(2mₑeV) when computing the electron de Broglie wavelength.

items.stem: In a medium-mass nuclear matter investigation, alpha particles (Z₁ = 2) of kinetic energy 6 MeV scatter from a spherical iron-56 target nucleus with proton number Z = 26 and nucleon number A = 56. Model the nuclear radius as R = R₀ A^(1/3) with R₀ = 1.20 fm = 1.20 × 10⁻¹⁵ m and nucleon mass unit u = 1.661 × 10⁻²⁷ kg. What is the estimated nuclear radius R, in femtometres (fm), of the iron-56 nucleus?

items.stem: Spectroscopic analysis of barium vapour in a flame-emission barium spectroscopy burner places the second excited state at −2.34 eV and a neighbouring bound state at −3.55 eV, taking free electrons at rest to have zero energy. Use h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. How much energy, in electron-volts (eV), is required to ionize a single atom from the second excited state?
items.workedSolution: Ionization energy from the second excited state to the continuum is ΔE = 0 − (−2.34) = 2.34 eV.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔE = 0 − (−2.34) = 2.34 eV (D).

options.label: B

items.stem: During an assay in a gamma-camera collimator test rig, background radiation alone accounts for 46 counts min⁻¹. With an iodine-123 source (half-life 13.2 h) fixed in position, the initial total count rate is 286 counts min⁻¹; measurements are repeated 26.4 h later. What total count rate (including background) does the detector record at t = 26.4 h?
items.workedSolution: Initial net count rate C₀ = 286 − 46 = 240 counts min⁻¹. Number of half-lives n = 26.4 / 13.2 = 2. Remaining net count rate C = 240 / 2^2 = 60 counts min⁻¹. Total recorded count rate = 60 + 46 = 106 counts min⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts background (240), divides by 2^2 (60), and adds 46 back to obtain 106 counts min⁻¹ (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides the initial total count rate directly by 2ⁿ without subtracting the background count rate first.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Correctly halves the background-subtracted net count rate but forgets to add the background count rate back to obtain the total detector reading.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Halves the uncorrected count rate first and subtracts the background count rate at the end.

items.stem: A sealed capsule in a targeted radionuclide therapy pharmacy holds 8.6 × 10¹³ unstable nuclei of lutetium-177 (T₁/₂ = 6.65 d), decaying exponentially over a transport interval of 9.11 d. What is the initial activity A₀ of the sample, in Bq, at t = 0?
items.workedSolution: Converting half-life to SI seconds: T₁/₂ = 6.65 × 86400 = 5.75 × 10⁵ s. Decay constant λ = ln 2 / T₁/₂ = 1.21 × 10⁻⁶ s⁻¹. Initial activity A₀ = λN₀ = 1.04 × 10⁸ Bq.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates λ = ln 2 / (6.65 × 86400) and A₀ = λN₀ = 1.04 × 10⁸ Bq (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Leaves T₁/₂ in d instead of converting to seconds when evaluating A₀ = (ln 2 / T₁/₂) N₀ in Bq.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor ln 2 ≈ 0.693 in λ = ln 2 / T₁/₂.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the decayed activity at elapsed time t instead of A₀ at t = 0.

items.stem: Relativistic kinematics in a linear collider positron-electron interaction region relates rest frame S to moving frame S′ (electron packet frame S′) boosted at v = 0.74c along +x. In frame S, opposing positron packet has velocity component u = −0.84c. What is the dimensionless velocity ratio u′ / c of opposing positron packet measured in frame S′?

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes u and v with signs into u′/c = (u/c − v/c) / (1 − uv/c²) = −0.974 (D).

items.stem: Observations of a solar-flare coronal magnetic loop detect continuum photoionization edges from six-times ionized nitrogen N⁶⁺ (Z = 7) in outer bound shell n = 5, where discrete levels satisfy Eₙ = −13.6 Z² / n² eV. Constants: h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What minimum photon frequency is needed to remove the electron completely from outer bound shell n = 5?
items.workedSolution: Ionization energy from n = 5 is ΔE = 13.6 × 7² / 5² = 26.7 eV = 4.26 × 10⁻¹⁸ J. Threshold frequency f = ΔE / h = 6.43 × 10¹⁵ Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates f = (13.6 Z² / n²)(e / h) = 6.43 × 10¹⁵ Hz (D).

items.stem: To benchmark nuclear stability in an alpha-cluster silicon-burning mass table, consider a bare sulfur-32 nucleus of nucleon number A = 32, proton number Z = 16, and nuclear mass 31.963294 u (mₚ = 1.007276 u, mₙ = 1.008665 u, u = 931.5 MeV c⁻²). What is the binding energy per nucleon, in MeV, of this sulfur-32 nucleus?
items.workedSolution: Neutron count N = 32 − 16 = 16. Mass defect Δm = 16(1.007276) + 16(1.008665) − 31.963294 = 0.292 u. Total binding energy B = Δm × 931.5 = 272 MeV. Binding energy per nucleon B / A = 272 / 32 = 8.49 MeV.

markScheme.criterion: Computes Δm = 0.292 u, B = 272 MeV, and B / A = 8.49 MeV (B).

items.stem: Vacuum-emitted electrons in a scanning electron microscope column gain kinetic energy across a 160 V accelerating anode from negligible initial speed. Assume h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, mₑ = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg, and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the de Broglie wavelength, in nanometres (nm), of the electrons?
items.workedSolution: Kinetic energy Eₖ = qV = 2.56 × 10⁻¹⁷ J. Momentum p = √(2mEₖ) = 6.83 × 10⁻²⁴ N s. De Broglie wavelength λ = h / p = 0.0971 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates p and λ = h / p to obtain 0.0971 nm (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 inside p = √(2mEₖ), computing λ = h / √(mEₖ).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the elementary charge factor e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C when converting accelerating voltage to joules.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Treats the massive particle as a massless photon using λ = hc / E instead of λ = h / p.

items.stem: Reaction kinematics in an electrostatic-confinement D–³He fusion chamber examine deuterium–helium-3 aneutronic fusion, where bare rest masses satisfy deuteron (2.013553 u) + helium-3 nucleus (3.014932 u) → alpha particle (4.001506 u) + proton (1.007276 u). Assume 1 u = 931.5 MeV c⁻² and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the rest-mass decrease Δm, in atomic mass units (u), in a single fusion reaction?
items.workedSolution: Summing reactant and product rest masses gives Δm = Σm_reactants − Σm_products = 0.0197 u.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Σm_reactants − Σm_products = 0.0197 u (D).

items.stem: In a photoelectric experiment using an ultra-high-vacuum polished nickel target, a clean nickel surface of work function 5.04 eV is illuminated at frequency 1.59 × 10¹⁵ Hz. Use h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the threshold frequency f₀ of the nickel surface?
items.workedSolution: Work function Φ = 5.04 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 8.06 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. Threshold frequency f₀ = Φ / h = 8.06 × 10⁻¹⁹ / (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴) = 1.22 × 10¹⁵ Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates f₀ = Φ / h = 1.22 × 10¹⁵ Hz (C).

items.stem: Along the tropospheric descent path of rest-frame length L₀ = 9940 m in a sea-level scintillator array, ultra-relativistic stratospheric muons coast at uniform velocity v = 0.98c with muon rest-frame decay lifetime Δt₀ = 2.38 × 10⁻⁶ s. What contracted length L of the baseline L₀ is measured in the moving rest frame?
items.workedSolution: Lorentz factor γ = 1 / √(1 − 0.98²) = 5.03. Contracted length L = L₀ / γ = 9940 / 5.03 = 1.98 × 10³ m.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates γ = 5.03 and L = L₀ / γ = 1.98 × 10³ m (A).

items.stem: Inside a barium-coated electron-tube emitter, a barium cathode (work function 2.52 eV) absorbs 173 nm photons in vacuum. Use h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, and mₑ = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg. What is the threshold wavelength λ₀ above which no photoelectrons are emitted from this barium surface?
items.workedSolution: Threshold wavelength λ₀ = hc / Φ = (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ × 3.00 × 10⁸) / (2.52 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹) = 493 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates λ₀ = hc / Φ = 493 nm (A).

items.stem: During a rubidium-82 myocardial perfusion generator parent, weak quark-flavour transitions (purely weak beta-plus transitions (u → d + e⁺ + νₑ)) convert a parent strontium nucleus with A = 82, Z = 38 into a product nucleus with A = 82, Z = 36. What is the signed net change in neutron number ΔN = N_final − N_parent across the sequence?
items.workedSolution: Initial neutron number N₀ = 82 − 38 = 44; final neutron number N_f = 82 − 36 = 46. Thus ΔN = N_f − N₀ = 2.

markScheme.criterion: Uses N = A − Z to obtain ΔN = (82 − 36) − (82 − 38) = 2 (D).

items.stem: Elastic 180° backscattering in a Geiger–Marsden evacuated scattering chamber sends a 6.9 MeV alpha particle (charge +2e) directly toward an immobile gold target nucleus (Z = 79, A = 197), taking k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻² and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the distance of closest approach d, in femtometres (fm)?
items.workedSolution: Initial kinetic energy Eₖ = 6.9 × 10⁶ × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 1.10 × 10⁻¹² J. At the turning point, Eₖ = k(2e)(79e) / d, so d = (8.99 × 10⁹)(2)(79)(1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹)² / 1.10 × 10⁻¹² = 32.9 fm.

markScheme.criterion: Equates Eₖ to k Q₁ Q₂ / d to obtain d = 32.9 fm (A).

items.stem: Nuclear stability mapping of a natural uraninite geological specimen connects parent uranium (A = 238, Z = 92) to product nuclide (A = 222, Z = 86) through a series consisting strictly of alpha and beta-minus emissions. What is the net change in neutron number ΔN = N_final − N_parent across the entire chain?
items.workedSolution: Parent neutron number N₀ = 238 − 92 = 146. Final neutron number N_f = 222 − 86 = 136. Therefore ΔN = N_f − N₀ = −10.

items.stem: A demonstration cathode-ray diffraction tube accelerates electrons across 2900 V onto nanocrystalline silicon membrane (atomic plane spacing d = 3.14 × 10⁻¹⁰ m) located L = 0.2 m in front of a fluorescent viewing screen. Modelling first-order diffraction via sin θ = λ / d and r = L tan θ (h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, mₑ = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C): What is the first-order diffraction angle θ, in degrees?
items.workedSolution: Electron wavelength λ = h / √(2mₑeV) = 2.28 × 10⁻¹¹ m. Using sin θ = λ / d = 0.0726 yields θ = arcsin(0.0726) = 4.16 °.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates λ = h / √(2mₑeV) and θ = arcsin(λ / d) = 4.16 ° (B).

options.label: A

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inserts an extra factor of 2 in the denominator despite sin θ = λ / d being specified.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 in p = √(2mₑeV) when computing the electron de Broglie wavelength.

What is the estimated nuclear radius R, in femtometres (fm), of the titanium-48 nucleus?

items.stem: A vapour cell in an interferometric krypton discharge tube contains krypton gas whose the ground level lies at −14.12 eV and whose adjacent bound level lies at −4.15 eV relative to the continuum threshold. Assume h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the longest wavelength of electromagnetic radiation capable of ionizing an atom directly from the ground level?
items.workedSolution: Ionization from the ground level requires ΔE = 0 − (−14.12) = 14.1 eV = 2.26 × 10⁻¹⁸ J. Maximum wavelength λ = hc / ΔE = (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ × 3.00 × 10⁸) / (2.26 × 10⁻¹⁸) = 88.0 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Converts ΔE = 14.1 eV to joules and applies λ = hc / ΔE to obtain 88.0 nm (B).

items.stem: A radiation detector in a hospital nuclear-medicine dispenser operates in a steady background of 26 counts min⁻¹. A fresh technetium-99m specimen with half-life 6 h gives an initial uncorrected reading of 1146 counts min⁻¹. Consider the detector response after 30 h. What total count rate (including background) does the detector record at t = 30 h?
items.workedSolution: Initial net count rate C₀ = 1146 − 26 = 1120 counts min⁻¹. Number of half-lives n = 30 / 6 = 5. Remaining net count rate C = 1120 / 2^5 = 35.000000000000014 counts min⁻¹. Total recorded count rate = 35.000000000000014 + 26 = 61.0 counts min⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts background (1120), divides by 2^5 (35.000000000000014), and adds 26 back to obtain 61.0 counts min⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides the initial total count rate directly by 2ⁿ without subtracting the background count rate first.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Correctly halves the background-subtracted net count rate but forgets to add the background count rate back to obtain the total detector reading.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides the net count rate by 2n instead of 2ⁿ.

items.stem: Quality-assurance logs in a hospital radioiodine therapy ward record an initial population of 2.4 × 10¹³ iodine-131 nuclei with half-life 8.02 d. Consider the source after 7.3 d of continuous exponential decay. What is the activity of the sample, in becquerels (Bq), at t = 7.3 d?
items.workedSolution: T₁/₂ = 8.02 × 86400 = 6.93 × 10⁵ s, so λ = ln 2 / T₁/₂ = 1.00 × 10⁻⁶ s⁻¹. Initial activity A₀ = λN₀ = 2.40 × 10⁷ Bq. At t = 7.3 d, A = A₀ e^(−λt) = 1.28 × 10⁷ Bq.

markScheme.criterion: Converts T₁/₂ to seconds, finds A₀ = λN₀, and evaluates A = A₀ e^(−λt) = 1.28 × 10⁷ Bq (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Fails to convert half-life from d to seconds (× 86400) when computing A = λN in Bq (s⁻¹).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the initial activity A₀ = λN₀ at t = 0 without multiplying by the exponential decay factor e^(−λt).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses λ = 1 / T₁/₂ instead of λ = ln 2 / T₁/₂ when converting half-life to decay constant.

items.stem: In a heavy-ion collider beam-crossing detector, observer frame S′ (gold-ion bunch S′) travels at v = 0.68c relative to inertial frame S. Simultaneously, opposing deuteron bunch has collinear velocity u = −0.58c in frame S, as depicted on the spacetime diagram. What is the angle θ, in degrees, between the ct′ axis of frame S′ and the ct axis of frame S on the Minkowski diagram?
items.workedSolution: On a Minkowski diagram with axes x and ct, tan θ = |v| / c = 0.68, so θ = arctan(0.68) = 34.2 °.

markScheme.criterion: Uses tan θ = v / c to obtain θ = 34.2 ° (D).

items.stem: Spectra recorded from an X-ray binary accretion-disc corona show five-times ionized carbon C⁵⁺ (Z = 6) whose bound levels follow Eₙ = −13.6 Z² / n² eV relative to the ionization continuum. Consider ions prepared in excited shell n = 3 (with h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C). What is the series-limit (maximum) photon wavelength that can photoionize this species from excited shell n = 3?
items.workedSolution: Initial level energy Eₙ = −13.6 × 6² / 3² = −54.4 eV. Ionization requires ΔE = 54.4 eV = 8.70 × 10⁻¹⁸ J. Maximum ionizing wavelength λ = hc / ΔE = 22.9 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Computes ΔE = 13.6 Z² / n² eV and λ = hc / ΔE = 22.9 nm (C).

items.stem: Precision ion-trap records from an accelerator beam-window nuclide evaluation report a bare aluminium-27 nuclear mass of 26.974395 u for A = 27 and Z = 13. Take mₚ = 1.007276 u, mₙ = 1.008665 u, and 1 u = 931.5 MeV c⁻². What is the binding energy per nucleon, in MeV, of this aluminium-27 nucleus?
items.workedSolution: Neutron count N = 27 − 13 = 14. Mass defect Δm = 13(1.007276) + 14(1.008665) − 26.974395 = 0.242 u. Total binding energy B = Δm × 931.5 = 225 MeV. Binding energy per nucleon B / A = 225 / 27 = 8.33 MeV.

markScheme.criterion: Computes Δm = 0.242 u, B = 225 MeV, and B / A = 8.33 MeV (B).

items.stem: Inside a low-energy electron diffraction (LEED) gun, electrons initially at rest are accelerated across an electrostatic potential difference of 900 V. Use h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, mₑ = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg, and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the de Broglie wavelength, in nanometres (nm), of the electrons?
items.workedSolution: Kinetic energy Eₖ = qV = 1.44 × 10⁻¹⁶ J. Momentum p = √(2mEₖ) = 1.62 × 10⁻²³ N s. De Broglie wavelength λ = h / p = 0.0409 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates p and λ = h / p to obtain 0.0409 nm (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 inside p = √(2mEₖ), computing λ = h / √(mEₖ).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the elementary charge factor e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C when converting accelerating voltage to joules.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Treats the massive particle as a massless photon using λ = hc / E instead of λ = h / p.

items.stem: Calorimetric analysis of an electrostatic-confinement D–³He fusion chamber evaluates the single-event nuclear fusion step deuteron (2.013553 u) + helium-3 nucleus (3.014932 u) → alpha particle (4.001506 u) + proton (1.007276 u) (take u = 931.5 MeV c⁻², e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C). How much nuclear energy Q, in MeV, is released in one fusion event?
items.workedSolution: Mass decrease Δm = Σm_reactants − Σm_products = 0.0197 u. Energy released Q = Δm × 931.5 = 18.4 MeV.

markScheme.criterion: Computes Δm = 0.0197 u and Q = Δm × 931.5 = 18.4 MeV (A).

items.stem: To calibrate a clean potassium vacuum phototube, ultraviolet photons at 1.09 × 10¹⁵ Hz irradiate a potassium electrode having Φ = 2.29 eV. Constants: h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the maximum kinetic energy, in electron-volts (eV), of the emitted photoelectrons?
items.workedSolution: Incident photon energy E = hf / e = (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ × 1.09 × 10¹⁵) / (1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹) = 4.52 eV. Subtracting Φ = 2.29 eV gives Eₖ,ₘₐₓ = 2.23 eV.

markScheme.criterion: Converts hf to eV and subtracts Φ = 2.29 eV to obtain 2.23 eV (D).

items.stem: In a fragment-separator hall, an evacuated time-of-flight beamline has rest length L₀ = 294 m. Passing fast radioactive beryllium-11 nuclei move parallel to it at v = 0.76c and have a nuclear rest-frame proper window of Δt₀ = 1.19 × 10⁻⁶ s. What contracted length L of the baseline L₀ is measured in the moving rest frame?
items.workedSolution: Lorentz factor γ = 1 / √(1 − 0.76²) = 1.54. Contracted length L = L₀ / γ = 294 / 1.54 = 191 m.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates γ = 1.54 and L = L₀ / γ = 191 m (A).

items.stem: Inside a solar-blind magnesium UV flame-sensor cathode, a magnesium cathode (work function 3.66 eV) absorbs 207 nm photons in vacuum. Use h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, and mₑ = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg. What is the threshold wavelength λ₀ above which no photoelectrons are emitted from this magnesium surface?
items.workedSolution: Threshold wavelength λ₀ = hc / Φ = (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ × 3.00 × 10⁸) / (3.66 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹) = 340 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates λ₀ = hc / Φ = 340 nm (A).
